LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. The defending World Champion Seattle Seahawks are coming to Mile High for a Thursday Night Football throwdown. It's a short-week turnaround for both teams, with the Broncos coming off a win and the Seahawks off a loss. Broncos-Seahawks was the Super Bowl many people expected last season before Bo Nix's shocking ankle injury. When the 2026 schedule dropped earlier this year, this game was circled as a potential Super Bowl preview. Despite both teams sitting at 3-2, few people currently view the Broncos as a true Super Bowl contender, but that's no different than the general consensus at this time last year. The narrative around the Seahawks, though, is strikingly different. What's the disconnect? Offense. The Broncos' offense and the quality of quarterback play haven't been at a Super Bowl level — but the season is still young. How will Broncos-Seahawks shake out on Thursday night? We're going around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff foresee this one playing out at Mile High. You can connect with each staff on X (their handles are linked next to their names). Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-1 : Another week where the Broncos decided to take the first three quarters off before finally showing up. At some point, it gets a little anticlimactic. That point, for me, is now. It worked against a winless, decimated Chargers team — even though Denver barely eked out a win — but it absolutely will not work against the reigning Super Bowl champs, who come into this game a little ticked off following a loss to San Francisco. Denver being home should help, but the magic won't be enough this time around. Fortunately, a much-needed mini-bye awaits. Payton might become the clubhouse leader for Coach of the Year if he can get this offense going. away.headline: Week 6 Injury Report: Seahawks at Broncos
away.blurb: Among those practicing fully on Wednesday was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited the previous two days because of an ankle injury. Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, does not have a game status on the final injury report, meaning he is good to go. Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. For the Broncos, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out with an ankle injury, as has starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). Starting cornerback Riley Moss, who missed last weekend's game with a rib injury, is questionable after being listed as limited in practice all week. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee, limited participation) CB Riley Moss (ribs, limited participation) Tuesday's injury report, which like Monday's is an estimation of participation, was mostly unchanged from a day earlier. home.headline: Broncos injuries: Jaylen Waddle, Jonah Elliss and Tyler Badie hurt on ‘TNF’
home.blurb: One of the first injuries was suffered by running back Tyler Badie, who injured his thumb in the second quarter and was ruled out just before halftime. The severity of Badie's injury is not yet known, but rookie running back Jonah Coleman ( ankle ) is eligible to return from injured reserve next week. On offense, wide receiver Jaylen Waddle ( shoulder ) left the sideline early to go into the locker room just before halftime. Waddle, who was announced as questionable, returned in the third quarter and finished the game. Fellow receiver Courtland Sutton appeared to have a slight limp after he took a huge hit, but he also finished the game. After playing on TNF this week, the Broncos have 10 days before their next game against the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 25. That extra time could prove to be helpful for the club's injured players. After a long weekend, Denver will return to practice and begin releasing injury reports next Wednesday. Broncos defensive lineman Malcolm Roach was evaluated in the team's blue medical tent late in the second quarter, but he returned to the game in the second half and ended the night with a team-high four quarterback hits. Elsewhere on the defensive line, D.J. Jones was spotted holding his left hand in pain, but he also finished the game. What appeared to be the most concerning injury of the night was suffered by outside linebacker Jonah Elliss late in the fourth quarter. After the play, Elliss limped off the field, favoring his right leg to avoid forcing the Broncos to call a timeout and stop the clock while the Seahawks were attempting to get within field goal range. Elliss was then carted off the sideline. Note that the replay of his injury is gruesome: We're still awaiting news on the severity of Elliss' injury. Elliss started Denver's first six games of the season while Jonathon Cooper was on the commissioner’s exempt list, recording one sack. Cooper was removed from the exempt list on Friday, making him eligible to play in Week 7. Social : Follow Broncos Wire on Facebook and Twitter/X !

Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be making the trip overseas for this week's matchup, and would be due to play a certain number of snaps. But how Harrison Jr.'s first game against the Jaguars could fare has the chance to go a few different directions. After all, it's a very quick turnaround for any player to make when being traded and dropped onto a new team in a week's span, and could lead to his performance in Week 6 being a bit more limited compared to how things might look a little later into the season. So how might Harrison Jr.'s stat line look by the end of Week 6's matchup over the pond? Let's simply predict how the Texans' newest receiver could do in his official debut, and break down just how limited he could be in the offensive game plan. Predicted Stat Line: 30% snap share, 4 TAR, 3 REC, 43 YDS, 1 TD DeMeco Ryans emphasized earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be involved in the Texans' offense as soon as this weekend. However, he also made sure to note that he won't be expected to play a super high number of snaps . "Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game," Ryans said on Wednesday. "But we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do." So just how many snaps could Harrison Jr. play? One outcome that could make sense is simply putting him in the role that now-former Texans wideout Jared Wayne had been in for the first few weeks. Jared Wayne and Marvin Harrison Jr. are vastly different talents, let's be clear. However, they are similarly big-bodied, outside receivers who can line up as a Z in several plays and situations, pairing pretty nicely next to the existing talent Houston has around the field at the position. But the numbers beneath those records leave room for a considerably less predictable afternoon in London. Jacksonville enters as a 2.5-point favorite after escaping Philadelphia 19-17. Houston finally broke through by beating Tennessee 26-3, then acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. These predictions deliberately push beyond a narrow upset or another respectable quarterback performance. The forecast: Houston produces its most complete game of the season. CJ Stroud throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Jacksonville's defense allows only 14 points per game, second in the NFL. Predicting four passing touchdowns against that unit is aggressive, but its strength against the run can obscure a vulnerable pass defense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Jaguars surrender 277.2 passing yards per game, ranking 30th. Conversely, they allow an NFL-best 63.8 rushing yards per game and just 2.9 yards per carry. Houston therefore has good reason to attack through Stroud rather than repeatedly challenge Jacksonville's strongest area. Stroud has already thrown for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions through five games. Against Tennessee, he completed 26 of 34 attempts for 261 yards, including an impressive eight completions on 11 pressured throws for 115 yards. The prediction requires Houston to convert passing volume into touchdowns, something it has not consistently accomplished. Harrison's arrival creates another possible weapon, although his debut and workload remain uncertain. This call rests primarily on Stroud's existing production and Jacksonville's passing-yardage vulnerability, not an assumption that the newcomer immediately dominates. Will Anderson Jr. records four sacks as Houston forces three turnovers Anderson delivered three of Houston's four sacks against Tennessee, providing the foundation for an even bigger prediction against Jacksonville. Four sacks by one player would be a spectacular follow-up, not merely continued improvement. The Texans limited the Titans to 187 total yards and three points after DeMeco Ryans reclaimed defensive play-calling duties. Tennessee's struggling offense makes that result an imperfect measuring stick, but Houston still ranks ninth in yards allowed per play. Jacksonville presents a tougher opponent, yet Sunday exposed pressure points. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception and lost a fumble against Philadelphia despite producing 331 passing yards and two touchdowns. Houston must turn disruptive plays into possession changes, rather than simply allowing Jacksonville to reset after sacks. The Jaguars' penalty problems could help create those opportunities. They have committed at least 13 penalties and accumulated more than 100 penalty yards in consecutive games. Backward movement makes passing situations more predictable, giving Anderson additional chances to attack. The bold call is four Anderson sacks and three Houston takeaways: pressure converts Jacksonville's mistakes into decisive field-position advantages. The Texans win by at least 17 points Jacksonville's winning record and scoring defense make a comfortable Houston victory the biggest leap here. The Jaguars have allowed only 70 points across five games, while the Texans entered last Sunday without a win. Nevertheless, a blowout becomes plausible if the first two predictions connect. Houston's passing offense attacks Jacksonville's statistical weakness, while turnovers supply short fields and prevent Lawrence from answering every score. Jacksonville also needed a 53-yard kickoff return and Cam Little's 57-yard field goal to escape Philadelphia. That extraordinary finish demonstrated resilience, but it should not conceal how close the Jaguars came to losing. Stroud's four touchdown passes power the offense, and defensive disruption keeps the Jaguars from turning their rushing balance into sustained control. London delivers a division-changing upset, not another last-second escape. Walker Little is expected to step into the starting role, creating an important challenge against Houston's pass rush. Jacksonville, meanwhile, can continue its strong start and maintain its position near the top of the AFC South. With Stroud looking to keep Houston's offense moving and Lawrence leading a Jacksonville team that has found ways to win, the London matchup offers an important test for both sides.

away.headline: The Texans Injury Situation Ahead of Sunday's Titans Game
away.blurb: For the Titans, Carnell Tate (back), Joshua Williams (pec) and David Martin-Robinson (hamstring) were all questionable. Tate and Williams have been cleared by Robert Saleh, while Martin-Robinson is still a game-time decision. Williams still has to be added to the active roster. Amani Hooker is out with a concussion. The Titans were otherwise free of any other injuries. The Texans have more than one game-time decision. Receiver Tank Dell is obviously still out with his knee injury. He was limited for two days of practice and didn't practice on Friday. M.J. Stewart (Knee), Blake Fisher (illness), Braden Smith (foot), Ed Ingram (illness), Aireontae Ersery (illness) and Kayden McDonald (ankle) were all questionable on the Texans' final injury report. Out of those players above, Ersery and Ingram are starters on the offensive line. Smith, McDonald, and Stewart would need to be activated from injured reserve. Fisher isn't a starter but could be one of the next men up if Ersery can't play. The Titans are definitely in better shape than the Texans with their injuries. The Texans Injury Situation Ahead of Sunday's Titans Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Texans Injury Situation Ahead of Sunday's Titans Game (Andrew Nelles / The Tennessean) Grant Bricker Sat, October 10, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans are meeting for the 49th time in series history on Sunday. The series is tied at 24, and something's got to give. Both teams are 0-4 and searching for that elusive first win of the season. The Titans and Texans have had many close games this year. Outside of the 23-10 loss to the New York Jets in the season opener, the Titans have lost the last three games by six points or fewer. The Texans are in the same boat. They lost a 36-31 shootout with the Buffalo Bills in their season opener. Then, they lost to Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 20-6. The Indianapolis Colts beat the Texans 19-17 on a go-ahead field goal with 16 seconds left. Last week, the Texans lost a heartbreaker to the Dallas Cowboys 34-30. Now, either the Titans or the Texans will get their first win on Sunday. Ahead of the game, both teams released their final injury reports . Tennessee has eight players on its IR. Fernando Carmona and Jackson Slater are the most recent additions. They joined Jaylen Harrell, Jaren Kanak, Dorian Mausi, Tanoh Kpassagnon, Milo Eifler, and Kendell Brooks. Injuries are going to happen in football. It's unfortunately a reality of playing at this level. The Texans are dealing with more than the Titans are heading into Sunday. That won't guarantee a win, but it's one advantage the Titans have. Kickoff is set for noon CT on CBS.

away.headline: Texans Announce More Bad News Amid David Montgomery Injury
away.blurb: The Texans cycled through safeties last season, even taking Pitre out of his nickelback role to help, but it has been their linebacker, running back, and wide receiver rooms that have been hit hardest this season. Getty Josh Buckhalter Mon, October 12, 2026 at 10:03 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The 2026 season got more complicated for Houston Texans running back David Montgomery in Week 5, despite the team's win–their first of the 2026 regular-season campaign–over the Tennessee Titans, and he is not the only concern. Montgomery was unable to finish the game, ending his day with 11 yards on five carries. Moreover, Texans safety Jalen Pitre was also unable to complete the contest, leaving head coach DeMeco Ryans to deliver a rather ominous update on Monday. "We'll see how he continues to progress, but right now we're looking at a week-to-week injury there with the groin," Ryans told reporters on October 12. "Jalen, same category as as Montgomery. He'll be week to week as well." This update only confirms what Ryans told media members postgame : "We're still evaluating him. He has a groin injury, may miss some time. And then with Pitre, we're still looking at his shoulder to see how significant that injury may be." Texans' Plans for David Montgomery, Woody Marks Unfolding This season has been rough for Montgomery, who entered Week 5 averaging 2.7 yards per carry, and ended with that exact mark on the season. A key trade pickup this offseason, there were already rumors that the Texans could start giving Woody Marks more work. Marks has a 43-149-2 mark on the campaign, including 15 carries for 62 yards in Week 5. "Woody did a great job yesterday," Ryans said during his Monday morning presser. "He had some explosive runs. Just made dynamic cuts, just played with great vision, good balance, just–he's done a great job all season as well. So, he carried that load for us yesterday and we'll continue to see more of that." Over The Cap's Troy Chapman shared a graphic on X to illustrate how much more explosive Marks has been compared to Montgomery this season. Chapman called it a "night and day" difference based on the eye test, and his data agreed. The Texans built Montogmery up to be a potential three-down option, but he has not even provided reliable production on early downs. That has allowed room for Marks to become more than just a third-down option, even before Montgomery's injury setback. Williams progressed enough for the Bears to list him as questionable for the game, but backup Tyson Bagent started -- and struggled -- in a loss to the Green Bay Packers. In fact, Bagent was benched for veteran Case Keenum after he threw a pair of interceptions in the loss. Chicago is now 3-2 this season, and it appears Williams is nearing a return from the hamstring strain (Grade 2) that he suffered in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings. According to Bears head coach Ben Johnson, Williams is "on track" and he believes it'll be "close" if he's able to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons. Ben Johnson on when Caleb Williams (hamstring) can return: "He's on track. We'll see if that's Atlanta or after. I think it's going to be close." So, it Williams isn't completely ready to return, the Bears may not want to rush him back for Week 6 with a Thursday game waiting in Week 7. According to ProFootballTalk's Mike Florio, Williams is still considered week-to-week , and that the Bears are waiting until he's "ready" before throwing him back into the fold. Williams was off to a great start in 2026 before his injury, throwing for 407 yards, two scores and one pick while also adding a pair of touchdowns on the ground for Chicago. Bagent has thrown three interceptions in his two starts for Chicago while Keenum threw a pick in relief of Bagent on Sunday. away.headline: Bears Friday injury report: Will Caleb Williams play vs. Falcons?
away.blurb: The Bears conducted their final practice of the week, which included final game designations for Sunday. Quarterback Caleb Williams practiced in full for a third straight day, an indication that he's poised to return to the lineup in Week 6. But Williams, who's missed the last three games, is questionable. There are some last step hurdles for him to clear, but all indications are he will be under center vs. the Falcons. Elsewhere, cornerback Kyler Gordon was also a full participant in practice all week, and he's questionable for Sunday's game as he looks to return from the PUP list. The Bears have also ruled out four players: linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring), running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) and linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad). The Chicago Bears are gearing up for their Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons, where Chicago is looking to get back on track after a brutal Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers . away.headline: Injury Update: Bears RB Kyle Monangai ruled out, QB Caleb Williams questionable for Packers game
away.blurb: Injury Update: Bears RB Kyle Monangai ruled out, QB Caleb Williams questionable for Packers game Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Molly Kaiser/Chicago Bears Bears running back Kyle Monangai has been ruled out of Sunday's game in Green Bay with a toe injury he sustained in last weekend's 23-12 win over the Jets. "We were certainly conscious of the thumb, and it turns out the toe is a bigger deal than we initially anticipated," said coach Ben Johnson, who described Monangai's status as week-to-week. "We've got him with a specialist and so we'll work through that. He's in a boot currently and we'll go from there." Running back D'Andre Swift was a full participant in Friday's practice and was not given an injury designation for Sunday's game after sitting out Wednesday and being limited Thursday with hip and knee issues. With Monangai out, fourth-year running back Roschon Johnson moves up a spot to No. 2 on the depth chart. The 6-foot, 227-pounder has rushed for 16 yards on four carries this year—all in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's win over the Jets. "Bigger body than the other guys in that room, and so I think he's a complete back. He can run hard in between the tackles. I think he's got enough speed to get to the perimeter. He catches the ball well out of the backfield and then because of his size, I think he's an asset in pass protection as well. So, he can do a little bit of everything, which we really value at that spot." Quarterback Caleb Williams, meanwhile, returned to practice on a limited basis Friday for the first time since injuring his hamstring in the fourth quarter of a Week 2 game against the Vikings. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest, though Johnson announced Monday that Tyson Bagent will start in Green Bay. Johnson said that it's "highly likely" the Bears will activate one of the three players who are on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list: Cornerback Kyler Gordon, defensive lineman Shemar Turner and Noah Sewell. All three are listed as questionable after practicing without limitations Friday. In other injury news, rookie linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad) has been ruled out of Sunday's game. FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. left the Atlanta Falcons' Week 5 game against the Baltimore Ravens late in the fourth quarter after taking a shot to the ribs. He returned one play later to attempt one pass on third down, but Penix did not take the field with the offense for Atlanta's only possession in overtime after a lengthy drive by Baltimore. Head coach Kevin Stefanski said that if everything goes according to plan, he expects Penix to start against the Bears in Week 6 but first wants to monitor his quarterback's injury throughout the week. When it comes to determining rep counts with the starters, Stefanski said, "I want to see how he's feeling. With any injury like this, you want to make sure, as they move around, how they are feeling. It could be all, some, none; we shall see." After practice, Penix said he took all of the team's starting reps. "I felt good today at practice. ... MRI/scans were all positive." Michael Penix Jr. said while its not always comfortable, he "made every throw today." home.headline: Atlanta Falcons injury report: Penix in, Henderson out
home.blurb: The Atlanta Falcons submitted their final injury report of the week on Friday. While the list isn’t long, it does feature starting cornerback C.J. Henderson, who has been ruled out for Sunday’s contest against the Chicago Bears with a groin injury suffered last week against Baltimore. Outside of Henderson, the Falcons injury report is pretty clean, with only defensive end Za’Darius Smith listed as questionable with a neck injury he’s been dealing with for a couple of weeks. Smith cleared concussion protocol Thursday, making him available Sunday if the team decides his neck is ready. Penix was knocked out of Sunday night’s game against the Baltimore Ravens after taking a big hit to his ribs. He was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa, who threw a game-sealing interception in a losing effort in overtime. “I hated it,” Penix said of being on the sideline during the game’s final moments. “I hated that I couldn’t get back in that game. With Henderson sidelined, Atlanta will turn to Mike Hughes and Avieon Terrell for help on the outside this week against the Bears. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich expressed confidence in those guys on Thursday, foreshadowing Henderson’s anticipated absence this weekend. As expected, quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has been removed from the injury report and heads into the weekend with no injury designation and will play against the Bears. Here’s the Chicago Bears’ injury report for Sunday’s contest. MORE: Chicago Bears Injury Report Atlanta Falcons Week 6 Injury Report

FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. — Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. left the Atlanta Falcons' Week 5 game against the Baltimore Ravens late in the fourth quarter after taking a shot to the ribs. He returned one play later to attempt one pass on third down, but Penix did not take the field with the offense for Atlanta's only possession in overtime after a lengthy drive by Baltimore. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. There has been a ton of movement in the odds for this game between the Ravens and Browns, as oddsmakers are gauging whether or not the two-time league MVP will play. Sports Illustrated spoke with several oddsmakers to give bettors some insight into how the spread for this game is currently set, and where it could move if Jackson doesn’t play. “The line this week indicates Jackson is around 60/40 to go and a revision will be made one way or the other once we know more on his status,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “There were no adjustments made with the Ravens winning on Sunday night, since backups don’t usually play as well in back-to-back games as opponents have more time to prepare.” After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved quite a bit toward Baltimore. The Ravens were 4.5-point favorites early in the week and moved as far as 5.5-point favorites at home books after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday that Jackson had a “realistic” chance to play against Cleveland. However, the star quarterback then missed practice, causing some books to adjust the line towards the Browns. “We're sitting at five on our site,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated on Wednesday. “As it currently stands as of this moment, and as Lamar's status becomes murkier, that will likely go further towards the Browns.” Still, the opening number that books shared baked in an expectation for the two-time MVP to play. Jackson’s injury isn’t considered to be a long-term issue, and he’s been one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL when he’s been able to take the field in 2026. In his four games in the 2026 campaign, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes in 2026 for 967 yards, six scores and one pick while adding 18 carries for 144 yards and a score on the ground. "Looking at this line, we are expecting Lamar to play," Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated . "It will drop to under three if Lamar ends up being out. No change for Baltimore, Snoop (Huntley) is a capable backup who has similar strengths to Lamar. They do not need to change their offense when Lamar is out, which is very helpful." While BetMGM has priced Sunday’s game with the expectation that Jackson will be in the lineup, not every book has done so. FanDuel considers Jackson “questionable” in Week 6, yet it still has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites on Thursday. “We are pricing the Browns Ravens game as if Lamar is truly questionable to play,” a FanDuel trader told Sports Illustrated. “If he is announced in/out the line will move to or away from the Ravens based on his status. Tyler Huntley's performance last week may affect this week's matchup with the Browns, but it will not change the outlook on Baltimore as a whole as their ceiling and range of outcomes is firmly tied to Lamar Jackson's health." Thursday’s practice for Baltimore will likely impact this line, as another DNP from Jackson would be a concerning sign for his chances of playing on Sunday. The Ravens are still capable of winning games with Huntley, who has completed 78.0 percent of his passes for 264 yards and two scores in 1.5 games this season. He’s also carried the ball 10 times for 36 yards and a score. Bettors that want to take the Ravens may want to wait for a more concrete update around Jackson’s status, as it seems pretty clear the betting market has set the spread for this game with the expectation that he’s more likely to play than not. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Lamar Jackson injury update, latest rumors on Ravens QB's status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
away.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. Adam Schefter of ESPN has previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game, with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the Ravens are "hopeful" Trey Hendrickson—who has missed two games with a thumb injury—returns this week. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. But the Ravens are obviously a much more dangerous team with a healthy Jackson.

home.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
home.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. home.headline: Lamar Jackson injury update, latest rumors on Ravens QB's status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
home.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. Adam Schefter of ESPN has previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game, with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the Ravens are "hopeful" Trey Hendrickson—who has missed two games with a thumb injury—returns this week. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. But the Ravens are obviously a much more dangerous team with a healthy Jackson.

home.headline: Browns Get Optimistic Injury Outlook Ahead of Week 6
home.blurb: The defensive duo of Mason Graham and Carson Schwesinger both returned to the practice field for the first time this week, on Friday. They both share a questionable game status heading into the weekend, but it's certainly a step in the right direction toward both suiting up against Baltimore. Graham has been dealing with knee and ankle ailments dating back to Cleveland's Thursday night win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4. The injuries kept him out of commission for last week's loss to the New York Jets, but could be poised to make a critical return. As for Schwesinger, he was seen leaving the locker room in New York in a walking boot and has been nursing an ankle injury this week. The reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year dealt with a similar situation last season, where he didn't practice the first two days of the week, then was limited for a Friday practice and wound up playing against the Jets two days later. Joining Graham and Schwesinger as questionable is star running back Quinshon Judkins, who has also been battling an ankle injury this week. He too returned to practice on Friday after missing the previous two days. Fellow running back Dylan Sampson has also been ramping things up after an IR stint this week. Sampson was limited on Thursday and Friday, but was ruled out. DE Derek Barnett, who is dealing with an ankle injury, is also listed as questionable. Two active players were officially ruled out in DT Mike Hall Jr (ankle) and G Teven Jenkins, who has missed each of the first five weeks of the season due to a back injury. DT Kalia Davis has been ruled out, as well. He spent the first four weeks on the IR, then had his 21-day practice window opened last week, but has only practiced once since then. Similarly, Dillon Gabriel has practiced every day since returning to practice off the IR ahead of Week 5, but also won't be activated this week. Now that I’ve regained your trust after my Packers-over-Bears pick came to fruition last week, do yourself a favor and take the new-look Texans over the London Jaguars. Houston gained confidence from beating up on Tennessee and landing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. C.J. Stroud tends to play at his best when Nico Collins is on the field, but now he doesn’t have to lock in on him with the arrival of Harrison, who played with Stroud at Ohio State. More importantly, the Texans’ defense is back on track, and that could present trouble for the inconsistent Trevor Lawrence. Iain MacMillan Week 6 Upset Pick Tennessee Titans (+260) vs. Indianapolis Colts It's time for the Titans to get their first win of the season. You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. I'll take Tennessee as my upset pick of the week. Peter Dewey Week 6 Upset Pick Carolina Panthers (-105) vs. Philadelphia Eagles This isn’t the craziest upset pick in Week 6 – Carolina is just a 1.5-point underdog – but I can’t pass up a chance to fade this Philadelphia offense. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, and the Eagles currently rank 30th in EPA/Play, 31st in success rate and 31st in yards per play this season. Only the Tennessee Titans (0-5) are averaging fewer yards per play than Philly. I think there’s a real chance that Bryce Young and this Carolina offense (eighth in EPA/Play, sixth in EPA/Pass and fifth in yards per play) put up too many points for this Eagles team to compete. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. Following last week's disappointing loss in Pittsburgh, the Colts dropped to 2-3 on the season and are in need of a win against the 0-5 Titans. But will they get it? Here is who the experts are picking to win this game. ESPN's three experts are all taking the Colts to win this game while doing so rather comfortably. ESPN's FPI prediction model also gives Indianapolis a 72.1% chance of winning this game by an average of 6.1 points. Pro Football Talk Mike Florio is picking the Colts to win 27-10. "The Colts can't afford to lose at home to a team that can't do much on either side of the ball." Pete Prisco also likes the Colts to win by multiple scores. 28-17 Indianapolis. "The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game." Almost a clean sweep. Four of the five NFL.com experts are picking the Colts to win. But Gennaro Filice likes the Titans -- here's why: "Admittedly, Tennessee has played like the most beatable team in the entire league, particularly on offense, where the Titans rank dead last in points and yards by comfortable margins. But Saleh's D at least has some bite, especially up front. Jeffery Simmons is an absolute force of nature, and while John Franklin-Myers has yet to validate his $63 million deal as a pass rusher, he remains quite effective against the run. Is it that hard to imagine the Titans containing Jonathan Taylor , getting just enough offense from Cam Ward and eking out a low-wattage win?" away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . away.headline: Colts Could Be Without Key Offensive Weapon Against Titans
away.blurb: Several key players appear to be trending in the right direction, but Indianapolis has already ruled out two contributors, and rookie tight end Tyler Warren remains questionable. Through five games, he has 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns, trailing only Josh Downs in receiving yards for Indianapolis. Losing him would be a massive blow to a passing attack that is already running out of healthy weapons. Alec Pierce remains on injured reserve, Darius Slayton was released Friday without ever appearing in a game for Indianapolis, and Dulin has now been ruled out for a second straight week. Will Mallory practiced fully all week as he works his way back from a thumb injury, although he is also listed as questionable while Indianapolis decides whether to activate him from injured reserve. Jonathan Taylor logged his second consecutive full practice, while Jalen Travis progressed from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday and full participation Friday. Grover Stewart returned to full participation after a rest day Thursday, while Charvarius Ward has now practiced fully on back-to-back days. DeForest Buckner did not practice Friday, but his absence was rest-related. Carlies being out for a second straight week still hurts a linebacker room that has struggled early this season, but Warren's status carries the biggest offensive implications. With an already depleted receiving corps, having Warren available could be the difference between an offense that finds its rhythm and another frustrating afternoon for Daniel Jones. Friday brought a mixed bag of injury news for the Indianapolis Colts ahead of Sunday's AFC South matchup with the Tennessee Titans. Of all the developments on Friday's report, Warren's status is easily the one that concerns me most. Tyler Warren Remains the Biggest Question Mark Warren was arguably the only bright spot for this offense in last week's 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh, catching seven passes for 83 yards and adding a one-yard rushing touchdown. That leaves Keenan Allen, Josh Downs, Laquon Treadwell and Deion Burks as the primary wide receiver options, with Warren's status potentially making things even thinner. Warren wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday, making his late-week appearance with a groin injury even more concerning. The good news is Allen and Downs have logged two straight full practices after lighter workloads Wednesday. Daniel Jones was also a full participant all three days despite remaining on the report with an ankle designation. Most of the Report Trended in the Right Direction Outside of Warren, Carlies and Dulin, Friday was fairly encouraging. Tennessee owns PFF's 26th-ranked coverage unit through five weeks, which should give Indianapolis an opportunity to attack through the air. But without Pierce, Dulin and potentially Warren, I am not sure the Colts have enough firepower to fully take advantage. That could put even more pressure on Downs and Taylor. home.headline: Colts TE Tyler Warren added to Week 6 injury report
home.blurb: Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren is now questionable for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans with a groin injury. He was not on the injury report the first two days, but appeared on Friday with the groin injury. Warren was listed as a limited participant. Along with Warren being questionable, so is tight end Will Mallory (thumb). Mallory remains on injured reserve currently, and with his practice window nearing its end, the Colts must decide soon whether or not to activate him. He was a full participant all week. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) and wide receiver Ashton Dulin (hamstring) are out. Any late-week injury report additions are always worth monitoring. Warren has been a big part of the Colts ' passing game, leading the team in targets, receptions, and touchdowns. His 213 receiving yards are the second-most on the team. Last week he had his most productive game, totaling 83 receiving yards. Along with what Warren adds to the passing game, he plays a key role as a blocker in the run game, and his do-it-all skill set opens up the playbook for Shane Steichen. home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Head coach Aaron Glenn’s team… Ezra Bernstein Updated Oct 16, 2026 2:41 PM EDT Pamela Smith/Getty Images Share this story The New York Jets will look to win their second consecutive game when they visit the New England Patriots at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. Head coach Aaron Glenn's team has already exceeded expectations, staying competitive in every single one of its games this season while claiming a couple of victories against the Tennessee Titans and the Cleveland Browns. Meanwhile, the Patriots have rebounded from a slow start, rattling off two consecutive wins against the Buffalo Bills and the Las Vegas Raiders to round out a 3-2 record. Moving past another divisional opponent would keep New England in contention for the AFC East crown early in the season. As many expected coming into the campaign, the strength of this Jets team is its defense. Rookie defensive end David Bailey already has five sacks while four other players have two. New York is yet to force many turnovers, but the offense has been so good at limiting its own that it has not been much of a factor. The only giveaway that the Jets have on their stat sheet is a lost fumble from rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, indicating a competent level of play from quarterback Geno Smith, who has managed every game adequately thus far. New England's defense will provide Smith with one of his biggest challenges of the season. Head coach Mike Vrabel's unit has forced six turnovers through five games, largely because of an excellent secondary led by cornerback Christian Gonzalez. It helps that defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr has created a scheme that consistently fools opposing passers, utilizing a variety of blitzes, rotations, and coverages to force offensive indecision on a snap-to-snap basis. With quarterback Drake Maye playing increasingly well, New England once again looks like a serious playoff contender in a crowded AFC. away.headline: Two key Browns players leave Week 5 against the Jets with injuries
away.blurb: The loss doesn't seem to be just in the standings for the Browns now, as reports come out of it that they saw both running back Quinshon Judkins and linebacker Carson Schqesinger leave in walking boots. Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot was the one to share this information after the game. On Monday, we didn't have an update on Judkins, but NFL Media's Ian Rapoport shared one on Schwesinger. He posted on social media, saying, "Browns star LB Carson Schwesinger suffered a Grade 1 ankle sprain in their loss against the Jets, though the injury occurred before his strip sack of Geno Smith, sources say. He is not ruled out for this week, though availability depends on how he responds." The idea of the Browns' defense losing Schwesinger for any amount of time would be devastating. The team has the Baltimore Ravens next up on the schedule, who are dealing with injuries of their own, but they need him for them and more.
