away.headline: New York Jets Fudging on Adonai Mitchell Injury is Merely the Latest Instance of Team Obfuscation
away.blurb: The truth is out there. Except if we’re talking about New York Jets injury reports. Then it was revealed that Mitchell had undergone some sort of procedure on his hand, but details on the what, when and where remained classified. What we do know is that Mitchell is out of the New England Patriots game, the fourth in a row he has missed. The Jets kept him on the roster during that stretch, eating up valuable space that could have temporarily bolstered other areas. For years, the Jets’ official line was that the promising linebacker injured his ankle stepping off a curb. Years later, it came out in the Denver Post that McAdams was in a fight with a Chicago Bear. “A little street brawl outside a bar,” said McAdams. “I did fall off the curb, but I had help. I can still feel the embarrassment.” McAdams said that “The story the Jets put out, that I was accidentally injured stepping off a curb, was done off what I told them. ” In the latest bizarre cover-up of a key player’s injury, the Jets are playing it coy about wide receiver Adonai Mitchell’s hand. He allegedly injured it when he caught a finger in a teammate’s jersey during practice, a pretty incredible bit of improbable bad luck if true. The Jets didn’t immediately place him on injured reserve, a sign that they thought the injury was minor. They did say his finger wasn’t broken and later added that he did not undergo surgery. Head coach Aaron Glenn spoke about Mitchell as though he were facing a grand jury, declining to say whether it was a sprain or fracture. He did say “He’s progressing faster than we thought.” Whatever Mitchell’s injury is, it’s yet another case of the Jets giving public statements on injuries that cloud the truth or downright misstate facts. Take the story of star Oklahoma linebacker Carl McAdams. Drafted by the Jets in 1966, the team outbid the St. Louis Cardinals for the prized rookie. But McAdams wound up missing his entire rookie year in the NFL. Then there’s quarterback Brett Favre. The Jets omitted Favre’s injured throwing arm from their late-season injury reports. The NFL subsequently imposed $125,000 in combined penalties on the club, general manager Mike Tannenbaum and head coach Eric Mangini. Tannenbaum acknowledged that Favre should have appeared on the reports; the injury was a torn biceps tendon, knowledge of which would surely have shifted the Jets game plan and odds. Another example comes in 2006, when wide receiver Laveranues Coles was described as suffering “a little bang on the jaw” instead of a concussion. Coles played along: “Whatever (the head coach) says, that’s what it is.” Yet another case came in 2013. Quarterback Mark Sanchez injured his throwing shoulder in the fourth quarter of a preseason game against the New York Giants. The Jets claimed he was “day-to-day.” Sanchez actually had a torn labrum and was lost for the season after October surgery. Those are just some of the examples from the Jets’ long, strange trip. home.headline: New York Jets receive mixed bag of news on injury report ahead of crucial AFC East showdown against New England Patriots
home.blurb: The Jets will be without two important offensive playmakers against New England, but the return of a promising young rookie provides some much-needed optimism. Let's start with the bad. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that two key weapons on the offense, in both running back Breece Hall, who has a quad injury, and wide receiver AD Mitchell, who has a finger injury, have been ruled out for Sunday's game against New England. That's not how it played out. Hall sat out against Chicago, missed last week's win over the Cleveland Browns , and now he's going to miss a third straight game. Look, at this point, the Jets could have put him on IR and freed up a roster spot. They haven't done that, and for whatever reason, the team keeps holding the door open for a return that hasn't come. That's been frustrating to watch. I'm high on both of these guys. Cooper gives the Jets a receiver who can take attention away from Wilson on the outside, and Sadiq is a matchup problem for linebackers and safeties. With Hall and Mitchell out, the Jets need their young talent to step up, and this is the perfect spot for both rookies to show what they can do. Honestly, it's a little bit of both. The Jets got their final injury report heading into their first divisional game of the 2026 season. It's a Week 6 away matchup Sunday for New York against the New England Patriots. New York is down two of its top playmakers, but a pair of rookies is finally ready to help. That's a tough blow for an offense that needs all the juice it can get. Before I get to the positives, though, I have to talk about the Hall situation. Breece Hall's absence is getting frustrating Hall suffered his quad injury in Week 3 against the Detroit Lions , and the Jets labeled him “week to week” for the injury report. Now, I know only a few weeks have passed since that game. But when I heard week to week, I figured Hall would miss Week 4 against the Chicago Bears and that might be it. Losing Mitchell on top of Hall stings, too. Outside of Garrett Wilson, Mitchell has been one of the few perimeter options this offense can lean on, and his finger injury takes another piece off the board. Rookie reinforcements arrive at the right time Now for the positives, and there are two big ones. Rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. will be active for Week 6 after suffering an ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Tennessee Titans . We haven't really gotten to see him in a Jets uniform making plays yet. He made one play against the Titans and got hurt on it. Getting him back on the field adds a much-needed weapon at the exact position where New York is now short-handed. He might not be as good as Mitchell yet, but he is certainly going to help this team. The Giants are 20th in success rate and 26th in opponent success rate through the first five weeks. Let's also consider the level of competition each team has had to face. The Saints have faced the Lions, Ravens, Raiders, Falcons, and Vikings, whereas the Giants have had to play the Cowboys, Rams, Titans, Cardinals, and Commanders. Their recent three-game stretch has led people to believe they're a better team than they are. I'll back the Saints as slight one-point favorites. The Giants have only allowed 21.2 points per game, but I’m not letting that fool me as it's skewed a bit by the seven allowed to Tennessee. The Giants tied with the Washington Commanders in what ended up being one of the weirder games of the season. New York should have lost to Washington, so the fact that they tied is being taken as a win for the team. But the Giants know that they will need a better effort going forward this week as the team gets ready to face off against the New Orleans Saints at home. New Orleans will be coming into the game looking to stop the bleeding, with the Saints sitting with a record of 1-4 on the year. Both sides need a win this week for different reasons, and the Giants will try to remain perfect at home this season. New York can't overlook this Saints team despite their struggles this season; otherwise, the Giants could find themselves in a tight contest. Bleacher Report did game predictions for every contest this week, with Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford picking. In these predictions, every single expert went with the Giants to take down New Orleans. Much of this could be due to the Saints having their own problems this year, but the Giants have shown real promise as a team. Even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart going down with an injury, the Giants have been able to stay the course. Backup signal-caller Jameis Winston has held down the fort well for New York, showing that he can get this team to the playoffs. But the problem with Winston is that he has been very inconsistent over the years in his career, and the Giants know this from the first few weeks of the season. As he gets ready to face off against New Orleans, Winston will need to make sure to stay focused. Winston can be very turnover-prone at times, and the Giants can't afford any issues against the Saints this week. The Giants defense has been a calling card for the team this season, helping them win a few games. And going against an explosive Saints passing attack, the New York secondary will need to be ready to go. The kickoff for the game between the Giants and Saints is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey

(Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads I want to start this week's report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don't disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this class from doing much, but you shouldn't lose faith in this group. The players who have been in the game have made plays that are good starting points, and although development matters, it's not like those players have been bad. Jordyn Tyson's injury is annoying to say the least, but hopefully we can forget about that once he's back. Do I think this class is going to be like 2025? No, but in hindsight, I think he could be a nice, middle-of-the-road draft class. Now onto the players: DT Christen Miller Finally, Christen Miller was able to get into the game on Sunday, and eventhough the Saints could not win, he did well in his short time. Miller made big plays against the run, took up blocks from offensive linemen to open up holes for other defensive linemen and the linebackers to stop the run, and in my opinion, proved he should be the starting nose tackle. It wasn't perfect, but it was enough for the Saints to play him more. This should hopefully be the case against the New York Giants, and to stop RB Cam Skattebo, you need a big defensive lineman that can prevent him from carrying the pile. TE Oscar Delp With the Vikings sending blitzes nearly every play, Delp had to step up as a blocker, and he did. The Giants are also at the top of the league in blitz rate, so Delp will be a primary blocker once again. I do hope the Saints utilize him as a receiver, because Noah Fant has had pre-snap issues this season, and prioritizing youth should be the plan moving forward. Try something new. OG Jeremiah Wright Speaking of trying something new, I wish Jeremiah Wright would get some snaps, but now that pressure is on the organization to win, a Cesar Ruiz trade feels less likely due to the risk. If a coaching change is made, I hope the next staff will give Wright a chance. WR Bryce Lance Last week, I said that it's clear Lance is not ready for WR3, and the Vikings game only reinforced that. The Saints need to make the move and put him at WR4 moving forward so he can learn. I know I have said to prioritize youth, but I also want to prioritize Tyler Shough's development, and Lance is negatively affecting that. WR Barion Brown Brown is a similar spot to Lance, but it's also clear he needs to figure out the return game as well. His fellow former LSU Tiger, Zavion Thomas, is in nearly the exact same spot with the Bears, but due to their offensive struggles with Caleb Williams being out, they have begun to utilize Thomas more. In addition, Thomas has improved as their main return man. Hopefully, the same can happen for Brown. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson was thrown to the wolves trying to block the Vikings blitz, and although I felt he did a decent job, he did have a holding call on one of the plays. As a rusher, Donaldson did exactly what I thought, picking up tough yards that did help the Saints in their run game. Against the Giants, I want him to be included once again. OT Mason Murphy In probably the most confusing moment of the game, which is saying a lot, the Saints put in Mason Murphy on a random drive, then subbed him out for Asim Richards the next. At first, I thought Richards got injured, but Moore said after the game that it was planned. I actually thought Richards did better than usual, and Murphy wasn't great when he came in. I don't think the Saints will make this substitution again. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was back last game, which was nice to see, but his involvement was limited. I wouldn't be shocked if that changes after Jayden Price's release being cut, so Styles Jr. could be the return man next to Brown against the Giants. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson

picks.blurb: Latest Teams On Air Listen + Watch Contests Events More LISTEN LIVE Home The New York Giants, coming off one of the most bizarre ties in National Football League history, are preparing to host the New Orleans Saints in Week 6 of the… Kurt Boyer Updated Oct 16, 2026 2:40 PM EDT Scott Taetsch/Getty Images Share this story The New York Giants, coming off one of the most bizarre ties in National Football League history, are preparing to host the New Orleans Saints in Week 6 of the 2026-27 season at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. Last weekend's Giants finish had to be seen to be believed. Washington, having driven into field-goal range at the end of overtime, refused to take any measures to stop the game clock with the score deadlocked at 27-27. Washington lined up for a snap at the :15 second mark without any timeouts in its arsenal, but QB Jayden Daniels ran a clock-killing quarterback sneak, a play-call so illogical that Commanders head coach Dan Quinn could potentially be fired over it. New York celebrated a zany escape and a three-game unbeaten streak. It's a weird way to get to 3-1-1, but this season's more successful of two Harbaughs will take it. New York is a home-field betting favorite over New Orleans, a 1-4 brand that is dealing with more injury woes at an unlucky time. New York wants New Orleans to wear Sunday;s bruises when the Saints leave for Paris. New Orleans Saints at New York Giants Betting Trends The New York Giants are on a four-game winning streak on home turf. The Saints are unbeaten in regulation in two road games this season. Betting totals have gone under in each of the prior three meetings. New Orleans Saints at New York Giants Injury Reports New Orleans Saints Linebacker Kaden Elliss is questionable with a calf injury. Running back Alvin Kamara is questionable with a back injury. Defensive end Tyree Wilson is questionable with an ankle injury. Wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is out with a hamstring injury. Running back Ty Chandler is out with a knee injury. Offensive tackle Kelvin Banks, Jr. is out with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle Bryan Breese is out with an ACL injury. New York Giants Tight end Theo Johnson is questionable with a neck injury. Wide receiver Darnell Mooney is questionable with a neck injury. Linebacker Abdul Carter is questionable with a calf injury. Cornerback Colton Hood is questionable with a concussion. Defensive end Chauncey Golston is out with a neck injury. Wide receiver Braxton Berrios is out with a foot injury. Quarterback Jaxson Dart is out with a knee injury. Linebacker Brian Burns is out with an ACL injury. New Orleans Saints at New York Giants Predictions and Picks The Giants are a different team than they were last October, when the Saints defeated the Big Blue 26-14 in New Orleans. Ironically, Giants starting quarterback Jaxson Dart was healthy at that time, and yet there's no denying New York is in better form now than it was at this time last fall, despite the QB injury. New York is ranking top-10 in the league in pass defense. Simultaneously, QB Jameis Winston has confidence from his vastly improved effort in Washington, having gone 33-for-54 with three TDs. Newly-acquired backup JJ McCarthy is a Big Blue package QB. So, why are the Giants only slender favorites to win at home? It can't be because of New Orleans' injury report. Saints QB Tyler Shough is ailing, unable to throw to injured first-round draft pick Jordyn Tyson in any event, since Tyson is still “recovering from a hamstring injury,” according to Erik C. Anderson from Yahoo Sports . Head coach Kellen Moore is under fire for the look of New Orleans' offense, which is rushing for just 81.8 yards per game. WR Chris Olave's 39 catches stand out as a bright spot. RB Alvin Kamara has been limited in practice this week. Bookmakers believe that the Giants have a flaky QB and a lack of run defense, and they're ready to take bets from overzealous gamblers led by the Big Apple's hype machine. The only problem is that the Giants are, in fact, this Sunday's superior side and the one with the momentum. New York Giants ATS is the way to go. away.blurb: That original timeline now approaches its two-month mark, but Tyson still isn't ready to return to practice. The rookie began the regular season on injured reserve, meaning he had to miss at least the first four games before becoming eligible to return. That minimum absence has passed, but his recovery has yet to reach the point where the Saints are comfortable allowing him to practice. Moore's announcement does not establish a new timetable for Tyson's return or indicate that he suffered another setback. With Tyson ruled out of practice this week, a debut against New York is effectively off the table. Whether he can return in time for the Steelers game will depend on his progress over the following week. That creates a potentially useful recovery window if Tyson cannot return before the team's trip to Paris, although the Saints have not identified a specific game as his target. home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Chris Olave Misses Second Straight Practice Before Giants
home.blurb: The Saints did receive some encouraging news, as edge rusher Tyree Wilson and defensive tackle Colby Wooden returned to full participation after being limited Wednesday. Alvin Kamara 's status also warrants attention after the veteran running back was limited for the second consecutive practice with a back injury. New Orleans' front seven faces depth concerns as Elliss (calf) and Anfernee Jennings (knee) missed practice for a second straight day, joining sidelined defensive tackle Shepherd (illness) and limited lineman Vernon Broughton (illness). However, Wooden (toe) and Wilson (ankle) returned to full participation Thursday. Those developments provide some encouragement for a defense needing its front seven operating near full strength. However, the Giants received encouraging news regarding wide receiver Darnell Mooney and safety Jason Pinnock , both of whom improved from limited to full participation Thursday. With New Orleans looking to rebound from a disappointing 1-4 start, the availability of several key contributors could play a significant role against the Giants. Perhaps the most concerning development for New Orleans is the continued absence of Olave, who missed practice for the second consecutive day because of an illness. New Orleans is coming off a frustrating 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in which its Tyler Shough and the passing attack failed to generate 100 yards and Shough also threw two interceptions. Losing its best receiver, who is second in the league in receiving yards with 537, creates another challenge for second-year coach Kellen Moore and his offensive staff. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team? High 58F. Winds NW at 5 to 10 mph. With the Eagles -1.5 at DraftKings , 94% of ATS handle is on them but 55% of bets are on the Panthers. There's heavy action on the Over with a low total of 40.5. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. The PPG is the fewest for Philly through five games since 2012, and the YPG the fewest through five since 1999. A juggled offensive line hasn't helped. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. They're coming off a brilliant upset win over the Detroit Lions, too. The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems. Despite that, they're not favored on the road, and some experts aren't willing to pick the Panthers to take the Eagles down. Expert picks for Eagles vs. Panthers in NFL Week 6 action Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts during the first half | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS," Dajani pointed out. Here's how SI's staff is picking the game: Albert Breer: Panthers Eva Geitheim: Panthers Mitch Goldich: Eagles Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers Conor Orr: Eagles John Pluym: Eagles Matt Verderame: Eagles Bleacher Report's Wes O'Donnell is taking the Panthers to cover the spread and win outright. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote. Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales reacts after the game at Bank of America Stadium | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. At ESPN , only Pam Maldonado and Dan Graziano picked the Eagles to beat the Panthers. The Athletic's Vic Tafur was obscenely blunt: "The Eagles are coming off two heartbreaking losses, they struggle against play-action passes (a Panthers staple), and it wouldn’t shock me if this is Sirianni’s last game as head coach." What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers. That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers. away.headline: NFL analyst picks Panthers over Eagles for Week 6 matchup
away.blurb: Besides being out of running backs, the other problem for the Eagles is that they've struggled to stop the pass this year and they're facing a Panthers team that is SECOND in the NFL in passing yards per game. I never thought in my entire life that I'd type out anything like that about Carolina's offense, but here we are. The deck is stacked against the Eagles, so I have no choice here; I'm taking the Panthers. PICK: Panthers (+1.5) 27-24 over Eagles However, the Eagles are far from healthy going into Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Their offensive line is battered by injuries, their right tackle Lane Johnson just suddenly retired and they're down to their practice-squad running backs. Carolina has plenty of injury issues of their own , but at least one analyst thinks they can pull off a win this week. John Breech at CBS Sports is predicting a victory for the Panthers: It's not a wild take given the situation. In fact, they were one Xavier Legette drop away from upsetting the Eagles the last time they visited Philly two years ago. Plus, the Eagles' struggling offense may not be able to take advantage of what might be the Panthers' biggest weakness—their banged-up cornerback room. Even without starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, Carolina might not have too difficult of a time keeping down the league's fifth-worst passing attack—especially if it's still missing their top wideout in DeVonta Smith. away.headline: Eagles get major DeVonta Smith boost ahead of Panthers matchup
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles finally received some good news, with DeVonta Smith set to make his return against the Carolina Panthers. Smith missed the last two games dealing with a hamstring injury. After starting the season 2-0, the Eagles have dropped three straight games and now sit below .500 for the first time since 2021. While poor performances and questionable coaching decisions deserve their share of the blame, injuries have utterly ravaged the roster. Highlighting the Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Eagles were missing five offensive players who started in their season opener. However, another major bump in the road arrived this week, leaving the Eagles’ outlook uncertain. The Eagles ruled out Jalen Hurts for Sunday’s matchup due to a superficial blood clot, with no clear timetable for a return. Smith has been a primary weapon in the Eagles’ offense since being selected in the 2021 NFL Draft, recording over 800 yards in each of his first four seasons. This season, Smith entered with a higher role as the clear No. 1 receiver following the departure of A.J. Brown, marking the first time he holds that title since his rookie campaign. The Eagles have leaned on Smith with success, with Smith on pace for 1,300 yards prior to the injury. Even after missing two games, he ranks second on the team in receiving yards and targets, only trailing Dontayvion Wicks. The Road Back to Full Strength Remains Bumpy A wave of reinforcements has finally begun to arrive, with Dallas Goedert returning last week and Smith back on the field this week. Saquon Barkley remains the last star weapon sidelined. So instead of catching passes from his longtime partner in crime, Smith will be working with Tanner McKee, who is set to make just his third career NFL start. Smith has shared the field with McKee in regular-season action only once, the 2025 season finale. Smith played just the first half of that game, catching three passes to eclipse the 1,000-yard mark for the season before taking a seat on the bench with the rest of the starters. However, Smith has a proven track record of producing when Hurts is sidelined. Most notably, during Gardner Minshew’s tenure with the Eagles across 2021 and 2022, Smith racked up 568 yards and five touchdowns over four games with Minshew under center.

away.headline: Panthers vs. Eagles Injury Report
away.blurb: "I know what I can do. I genuinely know what I can do. I know the impact I can have on this game," Greenard said on Friday. "I still feel like I'm one of the best at my position. I like myself against anybody. It's just a matter of me getting out there and showing it." The timing of Greenard's return is important as Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) is out and A.J. Epenesa (back) is doubtful. "Our injury report is longer than a novel. It's crazy, man. It's insane," Greenard said. "At the same time, we play a very physically demanding sport. When you're at this point, like we are with the Eagles, you're going to get the best from everybody. You got to make sure you bring it day in and day out. "Nobody is going to come save us, so we have to come get ourselves out of this hole. And we like that. We are not a losing team. We're maybe doing some loser things at times, but we're not a losing team and everybody knows that, so I'm excited to see what we do on Sunday." Wide receiver Hollywood Brown (ankle) and safety Marcus Epps (groin) are also set to return from injury. Center Drew Kendall was limited in practice on both Thursday and Friday. He's questionable for Sunday. The Eagles opened the practice window this week for cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee), tight end Grant Calcaterra (back), guard Landon Dickerson (knee), and tight end Eli Stowers (knee). All four players are questionable and would have to be activated off Injured Reserve in order to be eligible to play Sunday. It remains to be seen whether the Panthers will activate tackle Taylor Moton (lungs, blood clot) or defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton (neck) from Injured Reserve. Both players were full participants in practice all week, but are officially questionable for Sunday. away.blurb: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return Fans of the Carolina Panthers have finally got some good news regarding injuries. For the past four weeks, whenever the injury banner pops up in their feed, Carolina Panthers fans have covered and resigned, expecting to see their favorite player out for an extended period of time. However, this week, Dave Canales spoke to the media with updates on Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton . Wharton had neck surgery back in May, also putting him on an unknown timetable for his return. He was immediately placed on the PUP list, and the Panthers have tried to fill his role as the interior speed rusher. While there has been some success with Pat Jones, who has also missed time, there has been limited production elsewhere. Rookie Lee Hunter has so far been the most effective defensive tackle next to Derrick Brown, but on obvious passing downs, his slow pass rush has been a hindrance at times. In the same press conference where coach Canales revealed that Moton and wharton's windows were open, he also revealed the fate of Trevor Etienne, who began the season on IR. Etienne injured his knee during the final roster cutdowns, allowing Carolina to keep an open roster slot while placing him on IR. He is now ready to make his return. While his production was limited in his rookie season, sitting behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard, Etienne played well with special teams and passing situations for Carolina down the stretch in 2025. In a year where the Panthers again lost Johanthan Brooks to am extend groin injury, getting Etienne back to give Carolina running back room of three backs allows for Hubbard and Dillon to get much need resort during games, as well as a buffer in anymore unexpected injuries happen. Etienne will most likely return to his role in special teams, giving Carolina another player with kick and punt return experience to work with. The Carolina Panthers have been an injury riddle in the 2026 season. An early bye week came bearing fruit for the Panthers' injury news. Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton's return spells good things on the horizon for Carolina. Moton will allow Freeling to return to the development pool, allowing him to review his film, watch a Panthers staple on the right side, and learn from him. It will also give Freeling a chance to get healthier himself, after suffering a concussion and a knee injury in the last two weeks. Wharton's return means that Carolina might get a boost in pass rush. Wharton has always had the speed and strength to work from the inside, and adding him to a room with Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen means Carolina will have a perfect blend of speed and power. home.headline: NFL analyst picks Panthers over Eagles for Week 6 matchup
home.blurb: Besides being out of running backs, the other problem for the Eagles is that they've struggled to stop the pass this year and they're facing a Panthers team that is SECOND in the NFL in passing yards per game. I never thought in my entire life that I'd type out anything like that about Carolina's offense, but here we are. The deck is stacked against the Eagles, so I have no choice here; I'm taking the Panthers. PICK: Panthers (+1.5) 27-24 over Eagles However, the Eagles are far from healthy going into Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Their offensive line is battered by injuries, their right tackle Lane Johnson just suddenly retired and they're down to their practice-squad running backs. Carolina has plenty of injury issues of their own , but at least one analyst thinks they can pull off a win this week. John Breech at CBS Sports is predicting a victory for the Panthers: It's not a wild take given the situation. In fact, they were one Xavier Legette drop away from upsetting the Eagles the last time they visited Philly two years ago. Plus, the Eagles' struggling offense may not be able to take advantage of what might be the Panthers' biggest weakness—their banged-up cornerback room. Even without starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, Carolina might not have too difficult of a time keeping down the league's fifth-worst passing attack—especially if it's still missing their top wideout in DeVonta Smith. home.headline: Eagles get major DeVonta Smith boost ahead of Panthers matchup
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles finally received some good news, with DeVonta Smith set to make his return against the Carolina Panthers. Smith missed the last two games dealing with a hamstring injury. After starting the season 2-0, the Eagles have dropped three straight games and now sit below .500 for the first time since 2021. While poor performances and questionable coaching decisions deserve their share of the blame, injuries have utterly ravaged the roster. Highlighting the Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Eagles were missing five offensive players who started in their season opener. However, another major bump in the road arrived this week, leaving the Eagles’ outlook uncertain. The Eagles ruled out Jalen Hurts for Sunday’s matchup due to a superficial blood clot, with no clear timetable for a return. Smith has been a primary weapon in the Eagles’ offense since being selected in the 2021 NFL Draft, recording over 800 yards in each of his first four seasons. This season, Smith entered with a higher role as the clear No. 1 receiver following the departure of A.J. Brown, marking the first time he holds that title since his rookie campaign. The Eagles have leaned on Smith with success, with Smith on pace for 1,300 yards prior to the injury. Even after missing two games, he ranks second on the team in receiving yards and targets, only trailing Dontayvion Wicks. The Road Back to Full Strength Remains Bumpy A wave of reinforcements has finally begun to arrive, with Dallas Goedert returning last week and Smith back on the field this week. Saquon Barkley remains the last star weapon sidelined. So instead of catching passes from his longtime partner in crime, Smith will be working with Tanner McKee, who is set to make just his third career NFL start. Smith has shared the field with McKee in regular-season action only once, the 2025 season finale. Smith played just the first half of that game, catching three passes to eclipse the 1,000-yard mark for the season before taking a seat on the bench with the rest of the starters. However, Smith has a proven track record of producing when Hurts is sidelined. Most notably, during Gardner Minshew’s tenure with the Eagles across 2021 and 2022, Smith racked up 568 yards and five touchdowns over four games with Minshew under center.

picks.blurb: Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026 -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Aaron Becker Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:38 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A NFL analyst is all in on the Pittsburgh Steelers for Week 6. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? away.headline: Steelers WR Depth Gets Even Worse With DK Metcalf News
away.blurb: On their final injury report ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, DK Metcalf was listed as questionable to play with an illness. Pittsburgh is already down three receivers for its bout with Tampa Bay. Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was placed on the reserve/injured list, meaning the earliest he can return after missing the minimum of four games while on IR is in Week 10 following the team's Week 9 bye. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have also been ruled out vs. the Buccaneers after suffering their respective injuries in the first half of the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. The Pittsburgh Steelers were delivered another potential blow at wide receiver. Though it's an illness rather than an injury, which is positive news long-term for the Steelers, it's yet another instance of a receiver dealing with some type of hinderance. Metcalf was not listed on either of the first two injury reports of the week before registering as a non-participant on October 16. On the season so far, he has recorded 225 yards and a touchdown across 19 receptions. Now, Pittsburgh will take a wait-and-see approach with Metcalf before kicking off against Tampa Bay and hope that it doesn't lose another receiver for that contest. away.headline: Steelers Week 6 injury report vs. Buccaneers: What Rico Dowdle’s status means for Jaylen Warren fantasy owners
away.blurb: Add ClutchPoints on Google Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are dealing with several injury concerns ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , but one of the biggest fantasy football storylines centers on the running back position. Rico Dowdle is officially questionable with a toe injury despite practicing in full on Thursday and Friday, leaving fantasy managers waiting to see whether he will return after missing three consecutive games. Pittsburgh will also be without wide receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf), while DK Metcalf is questionable after missing Friday's practice with an illness. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey, cornerback Jamel Dean, and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton are also questionable. Safety DeShon Elliott remains unavailable with a knee injury. The receiving injuries could put additional pressure on Pittsburgh's remaining playmakers, making the backfield situation particularly important to monitor. However, Dowdle's potential return does not automatically make Jaylen Warren a risky fantasy start. Warren has been one of the Steelers' most productive offensive players recently, and head coach Mike McCarthy has made it clear that his role is not going away. McCarthy has publicly backed Warren , emphasizing that the running back is playing excellent football and that the coaching staff needs to continue putting him in positions to make plays. That endorsement matters for fantasy managers because it suggests Pittsburgh will not automatically return to the shared workload the team initially envisioned before Dowdle's injury. The Steelers' injuries at wide receiver could also influence how the offense approaches Sunday's game. Metcalf is questionable after missing Friday's practice because of an illness, while Wilson and Skowronek have already been ruled out. With Michael Pittman Jr. on injured reserve, Pittsburgh is running short on healthy wide receivers. Warren should remain the preferred fantasy option in Pittsburgh's backfield, regardless of whether Dowdle is cleared to return. Dowdle's two full practices are encouraging, but his questionable designation means fantasy managers should monitor his status through Sunday morning before making a lineup decision. Fantasy managers should not overreact to Dowdle's potential return. Warren remains the safer start, while Dowdle is a player to monitor until his workload becomes more predictable. Pittsburgh has a chance to make both running backs useful, but for now, Warren is the one fantasy managers should trust. away.blurb: When it comes to potential trade landing spots for Rudolph, there are quite a few interesting options. The Philadelphia Eagles , for example, are dealing with a major quarterback controversy as Jalen Hurts recovers from a serious blood clot. The Los Angeles Chargers just placed their top backup quarterback, Trey Lance, on injured reserve with a groin injury. The Washington Commanders, although they saw starter Jayden Daniels return to action, unfortunately had Marcus Mariota go down with a right knee MCL sprain. Rudolph is an important backup for Pittsburgh's offense, but his value beyond 2026 takes a nosedive. The Steelers would be wise to capitalize on the multiple quarterback injuries plaguing the rest of the league and get whatever they can in return for Rudolph. With the NFL trade deadline less than a month away, the Pittsburgh Steelers may have a few big decision to make before the important date. This is especially true when it comes to quarterback Mason Rudolph, who may be more valuable as a trade asset for Pittsburgh. The Steelers are swimming in quarterbacks at the moment, with two veterans and two young quarterbacks hoping to become future starters in the league. It's fair to assume that Aaron Rodgers isn't going anywhere, nor are the young options in Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar. Rudolph, on the other hand, could be enticing to other quarterback-needy teams around the league. Rudolph should easily be viewed as one of the top backup options at quarterback, appearing in 36 games and making 19 starts, as well as holding a 9-9-1 career record. He's also thrown for 4,925 yards and 30 touchdowns, in addition to having experience in multiple offensive systems. home.headline: Steelers Week 6 injury report vs. Buccaneers: What Rico Dowdle’s status means for Jaylen Warren fantasy owners
home.blurb: Add ClutchPoints on Google Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are dealing with several injury concerns ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , but one of the biggest fantasy football storylines centers on the running back position. Rico Dowdle is officially questionable with a toe injury despite practicing in full on Thursday and Friday, leaving fantasy managers waiting to see whether he will return after missing three consecutive games. Pittsburgh will also be without wide receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf), while DK Metcalf is questionable after missing Friday's practice with an illness. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey, cornerback Jamel Dean, and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton are also questionable. Safety DeShon Elliott remains unavailable with a knee injury. The receiving injuries could put additional pressure on Pittsburgh's remaining playmakers, making the backfield situation particularly important to monitor. However, Dowdle's potential return does not automatically make Jaylen Warren a risky fantasy start. Warren has been one of the Steelers' most productive offensive players recently, and head coach Mike McCarthy has made it clear that his role is not going away. McCarthy has publicly backed Warren , emphasizing that the running back is playing excellent football and that the coaching staff needs to continue putting him in positions to make plays. That endorsement matters for fantasy managers because it suggests Pittsburgh will not automatically return to the shared workload the team initially envisioned before Dowdle's injury. The Steelers' injuries at wide receiver could also influence how the offense approaches Sunday's game. Metcalf is questionable after missing Friday's practice because of an illness, while Wilson and Skowronek have already been ruled out. With Michael Pittman Jr. on injured reserve, Pittsburgh is running short on healthy wide receivers. Warren should remain the preferred fantasy option in Pittsburgh's backfield, regardless of whether Dowdle is cleared to return. Dowdle's two full practices are encouraging, but his questionable designation means fantasy managers should monitor his status through Sunday morning before making a lineup decision. Fantasy managers should not overreact to Dowdle's potential return. Warren remains the safer start, while Dowdle is a player to monitor until his workload becomes more predictable. Pittsburgh has a chance to make both running backs useful, but for now, Warren is the one fantasy managers should trust. There was some encouraging news, however, as running back Sean Tucker (quad) and cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle) returned to practice on a limited basis after sitting out Wednesday. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. (rest) was also back as a full participant, while defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson was added to the report with a rest designation. For Pittsburgh, cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton (ankle) were upgraded to limited participation. Running back Rico Dowdle (toe) was a full participant after being limited Wednesday. The Steelers continued to be without wide receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf), both of whom have already been ruled out for Sunday's contest. away.headline: Cardinals rumors: Arizona given gets coin-flip chances to trade Budda Baker
away.blurb: Rookie coach Mike LaFleur’s Arizona Cardinals are 1-4 on the season and ailing badly as Jeremiyah Love was ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Los Angeles Rams . Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis made a tough admission ahead of the game with his Budda Baker-led defense staring down the barrel of another potential beatdown. “I think the Cardinals will give him an option, like, ‘Hey, the Chicago Bears…I’m just throwin’ a team out there, want you to come play for their team, or Minnesota…Do you want to go?’ And if he says yes, then you move him.” Baker was selected by the Cardinals in the second round of the 2017 NFL Draft but his current team is looking far from a contender after five games and only one win. The offense has sputtered, receiving little in return after its long-term signing of receiver Michael Wilson, who was crushed by the team’s trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans. Related: Cardinals’ Jeremiyah Love officially ruled out for Week 6 vs. Rams Baker, an eight-time Pro Bowl safety, led Rallis’ unit with 11 tackles and a sack against the Lions, one of the few bright spots on a drab day at State Farm Stadium Glendale, Arizona. NFL insider Ari Meirov revealed recently that Baker could be on the move to another team based on what he’s hearing in the rumor mill. “If I gave you a percentage chance of Budda Baker getting traded, who has no guaranteed money, what would you say?” Meirov asked to co-host Johnny Venerable, who said he thinks Baker’s “time is up” with LaFleur’s Cardinals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Meirov compared the possible scenario to Kevin Byard’s trade from the Tennessee Titans, saying they gave him the option to be moved ahead of November 10’s NFL trade deadline. The Cardinals might be weeks away from having a fire sale, and Baker’s name could be included on the list of players finding new homes soon. Baker has played admirably for the Cardinals, but it may be time to move on based on the current circumstances. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. Allen doesn't have an injury designation, which means he's good to go against Arizona. McDuffie and Curl are questionable, making them the only players with game statuses for Sunday. The Cardinals already ruled out Jeremiyah Love due to an ankle injury, which leaves them without a top playmaker at running back. Tyler Allgeier will step up in Love's place, but he's not the dynamic runner and receiver that Love is. Budda Baker picked up a groin injury and did not practice on Friday, leading to a questionable tag for the Cardinals' star safety. Three others are questionable, including linebacker Zaven Collins. He missed Friday's practice with a hip injury. The Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals will play their first of two games this season on Sunday when they square off at SoFi Stadium. They both come into this contest a bit banged up, with the Cardinals missing one of their top playmakers on offense and the Rams still missing Myles Garrett. away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. home.headline: Rams-Cardinals injury report: Surprises for both teams on Friday
home.blurb: Additionally, Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl both got injured in practice on Thursday, raising some questions about their availability. Sean McVay said Friday that he's "feeling good about" Curl despite his questionable tag, and also believes Davis Allen is "trending in the right direction" with his foot injury. Allen doesn't have an injury designation, which means he's good to go against Arizona. McDuffie and Curl are questionable, making them the only players with game statuses for Sunday. The Cardinals already ruled out Jeremiyah Love due to an ankle injury, which leaves them without a top playmaker at running back. Tyler Allgeier will step up in Love's place, but he's not the dynamic runner and receiver that Love is. Budda Baker picked up a groin injury and did not practice on Friday, leading to a questionable tag for the Cardinals' star safety. Three others are questionable, including linebacker Zaven Collins. He missed Friday's practice with a hip injury. The Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals will play their first of two games this season on Sunday when they square off at SoFi Stadium. They both come into this contest a bit banged up, with the Cardinals missing one of their top playmakers on offense and the Rams still missing Myles Garrett. home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are set to enter Week 6 the healthiest they've been in weeks ahead of their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. While the Rams didn't practice on Wednesday, each player's status is an estimation. On the injury report Rams had only one player who was estimated to not participate. That player was tight end Davis Allen, who would have missed practice with a foot injury. Outside of Allen, the Rams only had five other players listed, with four of them limited. While Allen is the only player who was estimated as a non-participant, linebacker Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), wide receiver Alex Bachman (wrist), tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder), and cornerback Josh Wallace (shoulder) were all limited. Both Landman and Parkinson have been on the injury report over the last few weeks as they manage various injuries. The Rams have managed Landman during the week before the last few games and will likely do the same with Parkinson. Arizona had multiple players who did not practice Wednesday due to rest. However, safety Wydett Williams didn't participate as he goes through the concussion protocol. Additionally, safety Kitan Crawford and wide receiver Devin Duvernay were both limited. There are still a few situations to monitor throughout the week on the Rams' side, particularly at tight end with Allen and Parkinson. However, compared to where things stood over the previous few weeks, they are in a much better position from a health standpoint. With the Rams looking to get back to .500 against the Cardinals, having most of their key contributors available should give them every opportunity to do just that. home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable.
