picks.headline: Chiefs-Chargers Week 6 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
picks.blurb: Chiefs-Chargers Week 6 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Chiefs-Chargers Week 6 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp Fri, October 16, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Los Angeles Chargers , our writers predicted the final score and result. The Chargers may not have had the "Offseason Champions" accolades they frequently boast entering the season, but few expected an 0-5 start and making a case for the NFL's worst offense. They will try to get their first win on the road against a rested Chiefs squad coming off the bye. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists Kansas City as 8.5-point home favorites. When last on the field, the Chiefs were tested but came out undefeated against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Week 4. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) The Chargers' 0-5 start is perhaps the season's biggest development. Still, a division game should always be taken seriously. Yes, it would be easier to name the Chargers not on this week's injury report than to speculate on who might play through a number of serious ailments. Yes, Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh appear to be from different planets. But I'm going to plan a close game. Even if they play without longtime Travis Kelce nemesis Derwin James, I expect the Chargers defense to do what they've done for years: make this an ugly game that comes down to the fourth quarter. I expect Kansas City to come out on top, but I'm planning for a frustrating Sunday afternoon. Chiefs 24, Chargers 20 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) I did not expect this to be the season of the Chargers' undoing, but it has come at a good time for the Chiefs as they work their way back to the top of the AFC. The Chargers swept the Chiefs last season for the first time in nearly a decade, and Mahomes tore his ACL in the game that led to the Chiefs being eliminated from playoff contention. Despite the lopsided record and multiple players out, I still expect both teams to come out with plenty of juice. The Chargers to save their season, but the Chiefs will remind them that the AFC West still runs through Arrowhead Stadium despite the results of last season. Andy Reid off of a Bye Week is always an advantage, and his team will enter the game at nearly full health. With multiple starters out, I expect the Chargers to try to play the clock and play keep-away from Mahomes to help keep themselves in the game. The Chiefs offense will be without their key deep threat, Tyquan Thornton, but the combination of Mahomes and Kenneth Walker should be enough to get past the floundering Chargers. Chiefs 24, Chargers 14 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I don't see the Chiefs having much trouble taking care of business against the Chargers on Sunday. We already know Andy Reid's track record coming off a bye week, and now he's facing an 0-5 Chargers team that's absolutely decimated by injuries. On top of that, Justin Herbert is playing some of the worst football of his career. I expect the Chiefs to come out sharp, handle business, and win this one comfortably. Chiefs 27, Chargers 13 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chargers enter Week 6 at 0-5, making them one of the NFL's biggest surprises for all the wrong reasons. Justin Herbert and the offense have struggled under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, although the defense has kept them competitive. Injuries along the offensive line only make things tougher against an undefeated Chiefs team coming off a bye. On paper, Kansas City should win comfortably. But a winless division rival fighting for its season makes this a dangerous matchup. The Chargers would love nothing more than to hand the Chiefs their first loss. I don't see that happening Sunday. Despite injuries at wide receiver, Kansas City can continue leaning on Kenneth Walker III to keep the offense moving and create opportunities for Patrick Mahomes through play-action. Defensively, this feels like the week "Sack Nation" returns, with the Chiefs taking advantage of a depleted offensive line and making Herbert uncomfortable. Los Angeles will put up a fight, but Andy Reid's team will leave the bye ready to handle business. Chiefs 30, Chargers 20 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs are back to face another division opponent after the bye week. The winless Los Angeles Chargers come to town as the most disappointing team in the league after being a favorite breakout team for approximately 30 straight offseasons. They aren't untalented but have played poorly. That makes them dangerous at 0-5 with their backs aga the wall. Expect a close, bitter contest between division rivals, regardless of the records. Herbert will probably throw a couple of touchdowns, especially if his top 2WRs were back in the lineup. It's all going to come down to how well the Chiefs can execute. I expect the pass rush will get 3+ sacks. I expect Walker to have 100 total yards. I don't know what to expect from the Chiefs receivers. Will Cyrus Allen get a real shot? Will Xavier Worthy produce? Can they make up for injuries to Rice and Thornton? My prediction is that it won't be pretty, but it will be enough. Chiefs 27, Chargers 24 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) Throw the records out for this one. To me, it doesn't matter the Chiefs are undefeated and the Chargers are winless. Every time these teams play, it seems to be a battle that comes down to the wire. And despite being winless and at times inept, the last three losses for the Chargers have all been by a score. These teams know each other, and I think it will be another close game. I don't expect a full game from Rashee Rice if he does play, and this leaves the receiver room as a major question mark. Expect a big game from Travis Kelce and for the pass rush to finally get home multiple times against the Chargers' beat up offensive line. Chiefs 30, Chargers 24 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is a franchise vampire. He drains the talent out of an organization and gets as many wins as he can before they shrivel up into a corpse. Unfortunately, the Chargers were already halfway to hospice by the time he took the reins. In the end, Ol' Khaki Bottle Glasses will pin the Chargers 30th-ranked offense on offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel (AKA The Vape Prince) to buy himself another year. But how is the Chargers 22nd ranked defense Captain E-Cig's fault? The Chiefs are coming out of the bye. Despite being banged up at wide receiver, as long as they don't play down to the competition, they should take care of business. Chiefs 36, Chargers 12 Nate Christensen Chiefs-Chargers has been exciting for the past couple of years and had a lot of intrigue coming into the season. That is no longer the case, as the Chargers are 0-5 and a complete train wreck. There's a good chance the Chargers' entire staff gets fired. They're incredibly banged up on offense, and the whole unit seems checked out. Division games can get weird, but with the Chiefs off a bye and the Chargers facing this opponent, I feel like they should easily cruise to a win. Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) When a team is in as much of a down spell as the Chargers are, the Chiefs have no excuse to let them up off the ground. Los Angeles' incredible injury report, which named more than 20 players on Thursday, reflects how broken the team has looked over five games. Quarterback Justin Herbert hasn't elevated the team with his own play, so it's on Kansas City to do what it takes to ensure he doesn't get a bounce-back performance. That's what it will take to beat the Chiefs in Arrowhead on Sunday. Off a bye week, the team should relish this opportunity at home and take care of business. Expect defensive tackle Chris Jones to come off a bye week and lead a resurgent pass rush, taking advantage of strong man coverage on the back end to tally multiple sacks on Herbert in an imperfect victory that moves the team to 5-0. Chiefs 23, Chargers 17 2026 Standings Maurice Elston Dakota Watson Nate Chrstensen The AP panel was split in Week 4 between predicting a comfortable or a close victory for Kansas City . All nine staffers on the panel did correctly predict the Chiefs would win. Jared Sapp (34-31) and Ron Kopp Jr. (23-20) did predict three-point margins. Jared tied with Matt Stagner's 31-24 prediction to lead the way with only eight points of error. Matt has been the panel's overall most accurate member through the season's quarter mark. 92.4% of our readers predicted a Chiefs victory , with 60 .3% anticipating a close score. *To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

Kansas City enters the game at 4-0 after winning its first four contests, while Los Angeles is searching for its first victory after opening the season 0-5. The Chargers will have a difficult challenge at Arrowhead Stadium as they try to turn their season around against one of the AFC's early standouts. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Patrick Mahomes Leads the Chiefs Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has helped Kansas City get off to an impressive start in 2026. Through four games, Mahomes has thrown for 1,037 yards and nine touchdowns with just two interceptions, giving the Chiefs a productive passing attack. Kansas City has also found success on the ground with running back Kenneth Walker III. Walker has rushed for 537 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 6.2 yards per carry. His ability to produce explosive runs has given opposing defenses another major concern beyond Mahomes. Head coach Andy Reid will look to keep that offensive balance going against a Chargers defense that has shown the ability to pressure quarterbacks. The Chiefs will also monitor wide receiver Rashee Rice, who missed practice Wednesday with a hamstring injury. Justin Herbert Faces a Difficult Challenge For Los Angeles, quarterback Justin Herbert needs to help an offense that has struggled to produce consistently. Herbert has thrown for 937 yards, five touchdowns and seven interceptions through five games. The Chargers have averaged only 16.8 points per game, making offensive improvement a major priority. Herbert has the arm talent to challenge Kansas City's secondary, but he will need better protection and consistent production from his receiving corps. Injuries have complicated that task, with several Los Angeles wide receivers and defensive starters appearing on the team's injury report this week. Head coach Jim Harbaugh must find a way to help his team limit mistakes and sustain drives. A stronger running game could ease the pressure on Herbert and help keep Mahomes off the field. Andy Reid vs. Jim Harbaugh The coaching matchup adds another layer to this divisional rivalry. Reid has Kansas City playing efficient football on both sides of the ball, while Harbaugh is trying to find answers after a difficult opening month. The Chargers swept the Chiefs in 2025, adding extra motivation for Kansas City to protect its home field and maintain control of the AFC West rivalry. A Critical AFC West Matchup Kansas City has an opportunity to improve to 5-0 and continue building momentum after its bye week. Los Angeles, meanwhile, needs a complete performance to avoid falling further behind in the division. Mahomes and Walker give the Chiefs multiple ways to attack, while Herbert will need to deliver a more consistent performance to help the Chargers compete. With the Chiefs chasing another strong start and the Chargers desperate to get their season moving, Sunday's matchup carries plenty of importance for both teams.

away.headline: What is State of Chargers' Offensive Line Post Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater Injury News?
away.blurb: It is Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Los Angeles Chargers are already back to the same spot they seemingly have been stuck in since the inception of the franchise. They are down a plethora of offensive linemen, with always the best players being held out due to injury. This is the expected starting group after Rashawn Slater was placed on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. Joe Alt is listed as OUT with a neck injury, coupled with Kayode Awosika and Trevor Penning also being out with a fibula injury and a concussion, respectively. *It should be noted that Branson Taylor is officially listed as questionable, as he is coming off injured reserve. If he were to play, I would expect him to slot in as the left tackle, allowing Logan Taylor to play left guard in place of Alex Harkey. Jacob Spomer will serve as the team's backup center option, if Slaughter were to go out or were to need to move to a guard spot. Spomer was arguably the team's best UDFA, being one of few making the team's final 53 man roster. What is State of Chargers' Offensive Line Post Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater Injury News? Skip to main content SI.COM With that, the Chargers' injury report was as long as a CVS receipt, with offensive linemen being the bulk of what was listed ahead of the Week 5 matchup against the Denver Broncos and their elite defense. With all the injuries, what is the current state of the Chargers offensive line? LT: Logan Taylor / Branson Taylor * LG: Alex Harkey C: Jake Slaughter RG: Cole Strange RT: Travis Burke This starting group should not instill any sort of confidence in fans or even the rest of the team. They will also be going up against a Denver Broncos defensive unit that has always given the Chargers fits, even when their OL was in better shape. Slaughter and Burke should be solid in their roles, given that they have shown enough this season to be NFL-caliber players. As for the rest of the group...we can only hope to see flashes of NFL-level play to allow for hope for the Chargers OL depth in the future. The Chargers will also have two more bodies that they are expected to elevate off the practice squad, those names being Laekin Vakalahi and the recently acquired Daniel Brunskill. Vakalahi is the Bolts' International Player Pathway individual who has raw athletic ability but needs much more time on task, likely making him the last-resort type of option for the team. As for Brunskill, he is a long-time NFL veteran who has experience in the Mike McDaniel offensive scheme, starting five games for the Miami Dolphins and McDaniel in 2025. He is expected to be the first off the bench, knowing how to play all five spots across the OL, even if he was only signed three days ago . Published Oct 10, 2026 NATE GOSNEY Nate Gosney is lifelong Chargers fan and football nerd who has been writing NFL content since 2022. As a former OL/TE in a run-only offense, he loves some old-school, tough football. Gosney also earned an Associates Degree in Journalism

home.headline: Chargers Injury Report: Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston off report vs. Chiefs
home.blurb: Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were both completely taken off the injury report and should be ready to roll against the Chiefs. Fellow wideouts KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Brenen Thompson were both listed as questionable but both should also be in line to return to the field, though KLS still needs to be activated officially off of IR before Sunday. The other players listed as questionable are defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell, edge rusher Bud Dupree, linebacker Daiyan Henley, and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is the lone player with a doubtful tag. The Houston Texans just got their first win. The Dallas Cowboys can't get out of their own way, and the Buffalo Bills are mauling everyone in their way. It's been a wacky start to the season, which has made our NFL picks and predictions for every game each week a bit more difficult than I expected. We're having to adjust our perceptions and expectations on the fly, and we're still in the mix as we head into what should be a fascinating Week 6. Zach Rotman came out of the bullpen for me last week and came through with a solid week. Many, many thanks to him for helping the cause, but I'm back in the saddle now. Let's hope I don't make this thing go any further off the rails, but let's dive right into this fun slate with our NFL picks for Week 6 as we make predictions both straight-up and against the spread for all 14 games on the slate this week. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 6 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) The Buffalo Bills have been rolling, including toppling the Rams in overtime in Los Angeles on Monday night. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points - they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. It seems like Buffalo has to produce at this level offensively to win games because the defense is going to give it up. While the Raiders might not be a surprise contender, they still look like a quite competent football team behind Kirk Cousins and, while Buffalo will be able to score on their defense, they're still averaging 26.4 points per game on the year. I think Buffalo still has the offensive firepower against a middling defense to get the win in this game. But with it being in Vegas against a team that has a legitimate pulse, it's going to be another shootout and one that could likely be decided by a field goal once again. 5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Tim Crean, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:44 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills face off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. This matchup between the 4-1 Bills and the 3-2 Raiders gets a prime spot in the late Sunday window as one of the best games of the week. These two original AFC franchises haven't played a game with meaningful stakes for both teams since the 1993 "Just Freeze Baby" Divisional Round game . Now, as both sides come into this game with winning records, let's make some bold Bills-Raiders predictions. Start your Raiders in fantasy football The Bills are their own worst enemy so far this season, as they love to gift their opponents chances to stay in the game. Whether it is shockingly cavalier Josh Allen interceptions, infuriating James Cook fumbles, or the fact that the defense (outside of Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau) looks like it has no clue what it is doing right now, Buffalo loves keeping the other team in the game. Sunday will be no different, as fans should expect at least two turnovers from the Bills' offense and long stretches where the Raiders' O looks like the 2007 New England Patriots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means big games from the Raiders' defense, Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and maybe even the likes of Mike Washington Jr., Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker. So, for all you fantasy football players out there, any Raiders on your roster should be a good play in Week 6 . Josh Allen delivers again Despite the mediocre (or worse) play at times from the Bills' offensive line, wide receivers, tight end, and running backs, and defensive back seven, the Bills are 4-1 and leading the AFC East thanks to one man: Brandon Beane. Just kidding! He's the reason the rest of the team is struggling so much. The real reason is Josh Allen. Through five weeks, Allen is still the betting favorite for NFL MVP this year. Yes, Brock Bowers is playing great, and Patrick Mahomes is back, but if you define MVP as the players whose absence would tank his team's chances the most, Allen has to be the answer. Monday night's dramatic OT win over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams came courtesy of 210 yards passing and a staggering 121 yards rushing from the Bills QB. Sure, he threw his obligatory head-scratching pick in the first half, but in the second, it was a one-man battle with 53 Rams players, and the singular man won. Against the Raiders, expect more of the same. Vegas has an improved defense this season and an incredible pass rusher in Maxx Crosby, but that only means Allen will be forced to take off even more as usual. And with his receivers getting minimal separation and Cook's suspect ball security, it will be all Allen, all the time in Week 6. Bills 31, Raiders 24 This won't be a cakewalk for the Bills by any means, as the Raiders are one of (if not) the most improved teams in the league. We know Cousins is a professional QB, the Raiders have some incredible young offensive weapons, and Klint Kubiak seems like a legit NFL head coach with an incredibly bright future. Allen doesn't have those last two things, as his skill position core is the exact same as last year, as long as D.J. Moore is out injured and his "new" head coach is just the same offensive coordinator who couldn't get it done the past three seasons, but with a more impressive title. Nevertheless, Allen should be able to will his Bills to victory over the Raiders in Week 6 just by sheer force of talent and will. As good as Las Vegas has looked at times this season, they are probably a year or two away from being legit contenders. That's why we'll take the Buffalo to win here, and to do so by slightly more than the -5.5-point spread suggests. The Raiders, meanwhile, are 3-2 after suffering a 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots. With the Bills carrying one of the league's most productive offenses and Las Vegas looking to bounce back, Sunday's matchup at Allegiant Stadium presents an important test for both teams. Through five games, Allen has thrown for 1,249 yards and seven touchdowns while adding eight rushing touchdowns. His ability to create plays with both his arm and legs makes him one of the most difficult quarterbacks to defend. Allen was particularly dangerous against the Rams, throwing for 342 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 121 yards. His performance helped Buffalo survive a back-and-forth contest and improve to 4-1. Running back James Cook has also been productive, rushing for 532 yards through five games. His speed and ability to create explosive plays give the Bills another weapon that Las Vegas must account for. Head coach Joe Brady will look to keep the offense balanced while helping Allen avoid costly turnovers. Buffalo has committed nine giveaways over its last three games, making ball security an important focus heading into Sunday. Raiders Need a Strong Response Las Vegas will look to quarterback Kirk Cousins to help the offense recover from its disappointing performance against New England. Cousins has thrown for 1,269 yards and 12 touchdowns through five games, giving the Raiders a capable passing attack. Tight end Brock Bowers has been one of Cousins' primary targets, recording 312 receiving yards and three touchdowns. His ability to create mismatches could be especially important against a Buffalo defense that has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks. The Raiders will also rely on running back Ashton Jeanty , who has rushed for 291 yards this season. Establishing the ground game could help Las Vegas control possession and prevent Allen from spending too much time on the field. Head coach Klint Kubiak will need his team to improve its offensive line play and limit mistakes after the loss to New England. A Major Test for Both Teams Buffalo enters the matchup averaging 32.8 points per game, while Las Vegas has averaged 26.4. Both defenses have experienced difficulties, creating opportunities for the offenses to make an impact. The Bills will try to maintain their momentum after the overtime win, while the Raiders need a response at home to remain competitive in the AFC West. With Allen's dual threat ability, Cousins' passing production and two offenses looking to establish control, Sunday's matchup could be an important measuring stick for both teams as the NFL season continues.

Former Las Vegas Raiders first-round pick and current Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs received some welcoming news on October 16th. The NFL is removing him from the Commissioner Exempt List on October 19th, which means he'll be eligible to play in the Packers' Week 7 game on October 25th after missing six games. "The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Jacobs' arrest in May," the NFL wrote in a statement. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Stroud, Green Bay gets its ground game rolling against Dallas, and Justin Herbert breaks out of an ugly slump Getty Images Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 6 of the 2026 season certainly hammered home that fact. In the Denver Broncos (4-2) 17-14 "Thursday Night Football" overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , they triumphed at home despite averaging 2.9 yards per play. That's the fewest in Sean Payton's 318-game head-coaching career, and Denver's 168 total yards of offense ranked as their fewest in a victory since Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway's first start as a rookie in 1983. Quarterback Bo Nix , who ranks dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt at 5.6, improved to a 13-3 career record in games when he averages six yards per pass attempt or fewer, the best of all-time minimum 15 starts per CBS Sports Research, after averaging 4.0 yards per pass attempt on Thursday. All other active quarterbacks have a combined .283 winning percentage in starts where they average six yards per pass attempt or fewer. That's absolutely unfathomable. What other hijinks could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 6 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions. Packers run for over 100 yards for first time in 2026 vs. Cowboys The Green Bay Packers are back above .500 after quarterback Jordan Love's laser show (367 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while completing 25 of his 31 throws) in a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field in Week 5. Now that they have a winning record, they're now the owners of the third-fewest rushing yards per game (60.4) by any team above .500 through five games of a season in league history, per CBS Sports Research. Green Bay's NFL-worst rushing offense also ranks as the fewest rushing yards per game through games of any season in the Packers' 106-season franchise history. Some of that has to do with the absence of running back Josh Jacobs , who is on the commissioner's exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors, and some of that has to do with the team's beat-up offensive line. However, the offensive line has stabilized with veterans Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover stabilizing the team's guard play. That's one of the reasons why the Packers will run for over 100 yards as a team for the first time in 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football." The others are that Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd is a freight train at 5 feet 9 inches tall and 220 pounds, and the Cowboys have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game). Dallas allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to go off for 241 yards rushing, their most in a game since 2024, on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5. Facing a leaky defense like that and Lloyd fresh off running through Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson's face for a touchdown in Week 5, Lloyd and the Packers cross the century mark on the ground for the first time this season. Marshawn Lloyd trucks a guy on his way to the end zone 😤 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NNcSwQfTOU Marvin Harrison Jr. has first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is quietly playing efficient football: he has the fifth-most passing attempts without an interception (185) through five games in NFL history while throwing for the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL (1,402) this season. The Texans (1-4) have a high-volume passing offense this season because of their struggling rushing offense, and that will lead to Houston's newest player, 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , thriving in his team debut against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1). How much will he soar in his first game back with his former Ohio State Buckeyes teammate in Stroud? Harrison Jr. will produce his first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year in 2024 and just the third overall 100-yard receiving game of his young career on Sunday. He and Stroud were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history. Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston will be celebrating their newest trade acquisition's 100-yard game when the clock hits zero at Wembley Stadium on Sunday. Justin Herbert ends fourth-quarter turnover streak and multi-passing touchdown drought vs. Chiefs The Los Angeles Chargers are injury-plagued and riding the struggle bus at 0-5 to start 2026. Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions (seven) and turnovers (nine) in the NFL this season, and he has a couple of ugly streaks going against him. He has five consecutive games with a fourth-quarter turnover, making him the first quarterback since Charlie Frye in 2006 to do that. Herbert also hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns in a game in his last seven games, the longest such streak of his career. However, he will play a clean fourth quarter and throw multiple touchdown passes against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday. The last time the Chiefs were on the field in Week 4, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception on 31 of 52 passes in a narrow 30-27 Chiefs win. Herbert will snap out of his funk and raise his level to go toe-to-toe with Mahomes by having a clean fourth quarter and throwing multiple touchdowns for the first time in a while. Jets' Geno Smith throws first interception of 2026 at Patriots Geno Smith is on an incredible public relations campaign in 2026 with the New York Jets . After leading the NFL with 17 interceptions as a Las Vegas Raider in 2025, he hasn't thrown any through five games this season. Smith has six passing touchdowns to no interceptions this season, a stark contrast from his touchdown-to-interception ratio at this time a year ago when he had the same number of touchdown passes (six) but with nine interceptions. He is only the second quarterback in NFL history with no interceptions through five starts, after leading the league in interceptions the previous season, and is tied with Vinny Testaverde, also with the Jets, back in 2001, per CBS Sports Research. However, Smith will throw his first interception of the season in Week 6 at the New England Patriots . Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) is on track to return this week, fully practicing on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. In his first game back after a two-game absence, Gonzalez will intercept Smith for the veteran's first interception of 2026. The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year. The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved. These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings. Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? Here's what experts from different media outlets think. The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball. Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground. The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season. Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes. Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense. Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety. away.headline: Cowboys Injury Updates: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton, Joey Porter Jr.
away.blurb: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton Return After Injury Scares Lamb was hit on the same quad he took a hit to the week before, and it became painful, Schottenheimer said. Lamb exited with 8:32 remaining in the fourth quarter, was listed as questionable to return, and was back on the field on the same drive. He finished with 2 catches for 9 yards on 5 targets and played 34 of the Cowboys’ 60 offensive snaps. Cornerback DaRon Bland played all 72 defensive snaps with Porter out. “It affects us too much. A little bit, just missing a guy. You always wanna have everybody there, so. And to have a lot of guys hurt right now. So it hurts a little bit,” Bland said. “But we still had to go out there and perform.” Safety Alijah Clark left in the second quarter with a hamstring injury and was ruled out in the third quarter. Cornerback Shavon Revel was hurt on a third-quarter play and returned early in the fourth quarter. ‘Everything Still Out In Front Of Us’: Dallas Cowboys 1.5 Games Back As NFC East Goes Winless In Week 5 Cowboys Injury Updates: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton, Joey Porter Jr. Home ARLINGTON, Texas — Dallas Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb and left tackle Tyler Guyton both left Thursday night’s 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with injuries and returned, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was inactive after falling ill at AT&T Stadium. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer gave initial updates after the game. Four days earlier, Lamb set a career high with 17 catches for 189 yards and caught the go-ahead 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left in a 34-30 win over the Houston Texans . Guyton’s X-rays looked good, Schottenheimer said, but the Cowboys will run more tests on his back. Guyton played 52 offensive snaps, 87% of the total. Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said he did not know the seriousness of Guyton’s back strain, but that Guyton came back in at the end. Joey Porter Jr. Becomes ‘Very, Very Sick’ Before Kickoff Porter was a late scratch, and Schottenheimer said the decision came after the trainers went to the coaches before the game. “Unique thing. Came to the stadium and he wasn’t feeling very well. And trainers came to us, said it got significantly worse after we treated him,” Schottenheimer said. “He just wasn’t feeling good. And the decision was made that he wasn’t going to be able to play, as he was very, very sick.” Jones said Porter had flu symptoms and could not keep his food down. Dallas acquired Porter in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers last week, and Thursday was supposed to be his second game with the Cowboys, The Associated Press reported. DaRon Bland, Shavon Revel Among Cowboys Secondary Updates Receiver Jonathan Mingo was on the injury report entering the game, and Schottenheimer said a lot of people have had little things. Mingo played and caught 2 passes for 20 yards. Revel said after the game that he took a shot before kickoff and feels great. home.headline: NFL releases major update on status of Packers RB Josh Jacobs
home.blurb: The NFL removed Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs from the Commissioner Exempt List, effective Monday, making him eligible to return to the field for Sunday’s Week 7 matchup against the division-rival Detroit Lions. While Jacobs is now eligible to return to the roster, the NFL’s investigation under the league’s Personal Conduct Policy is still underway. Jacobs, who was arrested in May following a domestic disturbance, was originally placed on the Commissioner Exempt List before the 2026 season on Aug. 30. The NFL released a public statement following this move: “The National Football League today notified Josh Jacobs of the Green Bay Packers that he will be removed from the Commissioner Exempt List on Oct. 19. He will be eligible to play in the Packers’ Week 7 game on Oct. 25 after missing six games. “The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Jacobs’ arrest in May. The league’s review remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Jacobs’ roster status.” Without Jacobs through the first five games of the 2026 season, the Packers rank dead last in rushing yards per game with 60.4. MarShawn Lloyd has just 112 rushing yards on the season, followed by Kaleb Johnson with 106. The Packers will face off against the Dallas Cowboys in a primetime “Sunday Night Football” matchup in Week 6. home.headline: Packers' final injury report before Cowboys game puts 2 defensive position groups under the microscope
home.blurb: DT Jonathan Ford (out – calf) DT Javon Hargrave (out – Achilles) WR Skyy Moore (out – ankle) CB Benjamin St-Juste (out – hamstring) DT Jordon Riley (doubtful – Achilles) G Aaron Banks (questionable – knee/toe) DT Anthony Campbell (questionable – ankle) CB Brandon Cisse (questionable – hip) G Jacob Monk (questionable – quadricep) WR Savion Williams (questionable – ankle) Cornerback Keisean Nixon opened the week as a non-participant on Wednesday with a groin injury, but head coach Matt LaFleur had already confirmed in his press conference that Nixon will play. The veteran returned to practice on a limited basis Thursday, opening the gates for his availability against Dallas. On the other hand, rookie second-rounder Brandon Cisse was added to the injury report with a hip injury. He was limited on Friday and is questionable to play. Meanwhile, backup cornerback Benjamin St-Juste has a hamstring injury and did not practice at all. He's already been ruled out. The other position with plenty of reasons for concern is defensive tackle. Green Bay started the regular season with seven defensive tackles on the 53-man roster, but injuries have taken a toll on the group . Warren Brinson is on injured reserve with a groin injury. Javon Hargrave remains on the 53-man roster, but he is out for the season with a ruptured Achilles and is ruled out against the Cowboys. He will eventually move to injured reserve as well. Three more defensive tackles appeared on the report through the week, but Devonte Wyatt (ankle) is off the report and good to go. Jonathan Ford, who has a calf injury, did not practice at all and will not play. Anthony Campbell is also dealing with an ankle injurie, and he's questionable. Therefore, the only defensive tackles who are fully healthy going into Sunday are Karl Brooks and rookie third-rounder Chris McClellan. For a position that started the season as one of the deepest on the roster, that's a significant shift in a short period of time. The good news is that defensive tackle Jordon Riley is working his way back from an Achilles injury. He got hurt late last season and started this season on the physically unable to perform list, but the Packers have now designated him to return. That doesn't necessarily mean Riley will play against Dallas. The Packers first have to activate him to the 53-man roster before he can suit up. Will they dare bet on the 49ers to fail on Monday Night Football against the Washington Commanders? It's a big number, and an even bigger total. It feels weird to say this about a team that just scored 32 points, but the 49ers probably can't wait to face a Commanders defense that just allowed Jameis Winston a 50.8% success rate, three touchdowns, and over 326 yards. All three of the Giants' starting receivers had over 55 receiving yards. This should be the kind of game where you get your other receivers involved and build confidence for later on in the season. Washington's rushing defense is 25th in success rate for the season, but also 25th through the air. The large spread and high total suggest the 49ers will score early and often. Washington's offensive coordinator, David Blough, began coaching almost immediately after his playing career ended in 2023. He went from the assistant quarterbacks coach to offensive coordinator in two seasons. Jayden Daniels just ran for over 100 yards, and Jacor Croskey-Merritt is a big-play threat. When he's on the field, Terry McLaurin can be problematic. And the Commanders have just enough weapons around him to be dangerous. Washington has scored 22, 20, 31, 13, and 27 points. picks.headline: Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football
picks.blurb: Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Wed, October 14, 2026 at 1:54 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the Washington Commanders are likely playing with a lame-duck coach, the San Francisco 49ers will be without a key defender. These teams, going in different directions, will meet in Week 6 on Monday Night Football, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Still reeling from a last-second overtime mental meltdown in the 27-27 tie to the Giants, the Commanders carry a record of 1-3-1 and a heavy underdog role into this game. Meanwhile, the 49ers are flying high with a record of 5-0 on the season. They're coming off an exciting 32-29 win over the Seahawks, giving them firm control of the NFC West title chase. 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 300 yards The Commanders have been good against the run this season, giving up only 95.4 yards per game. They will have a challenge against the 49ers' offense, who are No. 8 in rushing yards per game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Look for the Commanders to slow, not stop, Christian McCaffrey. However, that opens things up for the 49ers' passing attack to hit high gear. The biggest problem the Commanders will have is Mike Evans. That's not a deep analysis. It's something every team faces when playing the 49ers. Purdy said Evans makes a big difference , according to ESPN. "He's a game changer," Purdy said after the win over the Seahawks. "True X receiver that, if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. "I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. So as a quarterback, any time I have an (opportunity) to go to him, it always feels good." Evans doesn't shy away from the attention. And why should he? He's a future Hall of Famer. "I do feel like I'm one of the best receivers in the game," Evans said. "I got a big frame, so if you throw it around me, I'm going to do my best to try to make those contested grabs." The 49ers won't have Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. That could allow the Commanders to focus more attention on Evans. But the 49ers still have threats, including George Kittle. And even Kittle has major respect for Evans, according to a post on X. "Mike Evans is really good at football," Kittle posted. 49ers TE George Kittle will have a season-high reception total Kittle's best game came in Week 3 against the Cardinals as he grabbed six passes for 82 yards and a pair of scores. Look for him to have a similar line against the Commanders with Samuel on the shelf. The 49ers have Kittle, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing on the roster. And that's enough , said head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to ESPN. "I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look." Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will finally cross 200-yard passing mark In three games this season, Daniels hasn't totaled over 200 yards passing. Look for that to change against the 49ers. It makes sense for the 49ers to focus defensively on keeping Daniels in check as a runner. He's coming off a game where he ran for 103 yards on nine carries and a pair of touchdowns. And look for the Commanders' game plan to lean more on the passing game than it has so far this season. Part of it will likely be from necessity as the Commanders figure to be chasing points throughout this game. Daniels has a lot to prove after his late-game blunder against the Giants. He has tried to own the situation , according to ESPN. "We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me." A bounce-back game against the 49ers by Daniels won't help Quinn's future as head coach. But it would be an olive branch to Commanders' fans who are furious about Daniels' mental meltdown. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin will get a long TD Look for the Commanders to strike deep against the 49ers. McLaurin should be the beneficiary with a 40-plus-yard score. McLaurin hasn't been anything special from a fantasy perspective this season. He had catch totals of 2, 2, 6, and 4 in his first four games. He has 203 total yards and one touchdown. Those aren't WR1 numbers. He is playing like a pedestrian blob so far this season. And while he probably won't juice up those numbers much against the 49ers' tough defense, it's not out of the realm of possibility for him to get a deep ball. How big of an ask is a 40-yard TD strike between Daniels and McLaurin? Consider that Daniels' longest pass of the season is 33 yards. McLaurin's longest catch is 30 yards. Those numbers seem to belie the likelihood of a long hookup. However, the 49ers can't fear the deep ball because of this duo's modest production. And that's why there's a window of opportunity for a bomb. However, look for the Commanders to fall to 1-4-1 after this one. They don't have the roster to compete with the 49ers. San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments. Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success. Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo. The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult. Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly. Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie. Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs. Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities. Kyle Shanahan vs. Dan Quinn The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game. Shanahan has San Francisco playing confident football, while Quinn needs Washington to respond after letting a potential victory slip away. For the Commanders, limiting turnovers and improving their second-half execution will be essential. The 49ers, meanwhile, will look to continue their balanced offensive approach and use their home-field advantage. A Major Test for Both Teams San Francisco has an opportunity to improve to 6-0 and strengthen its position in the NFC West. Washington needs a complete performance to show it can compete with one of the conference's unbeaten teams. With Purdy and McCaffrey leading the 49ers against Daniels and Washington's offense, Monday night's matchup offers an important test for both teams as the NFL season moves deeper into October.

Stefon Diggs, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, and Marcus Mariota did not practice as Washington got ready for its Monday Night Football matchup with San Francisco. He and defensive end Charles Omenihu (groin, ankle) were seen working off to the side, according to SB Nation's Hogs Haven. The secondary is thin too. Terry McLaurin was limited with a hamstring issue. With Diggs also hurt, Washington's top two receivers are both nursing hamstrings. Running back Austin Ekeler (chest), receiver Treylon Burks (shoulder), linebacker Jordan Magee (hamstring), safety Quan Martin (illness), cornerback Fabian Moreau (knee) and safety Jeremy Reaves (rib) were also limited. away.headline: Washington Commanders Get Good Injury News in the Secondary
away.blurb: Diggs joined wide receiver Terry McLaurin as inactive ahead of week five as both battled hamstring injuries, though McLaurin ultimately suited up with Diggs missing his first game of the season. Both Owens and Butler were also diagnosed with hamstring injuries, while Croskey-Merritt was limited with a groin injury ahead of week five despite ultimately playing. Omenihu was inactive in week five after not practicing in the days ahead due to a groin/ankle injury, adding a question when the free agent addition will be able to make his return to upgrade the front seven again. It marks the team's final game before the bye week with all eyes on whether the Commanders can secure the first win away from Northwest Stadium in 2026 while the team looks to climb itself out of the early hole after moving to 1-3-1 following the week five tie against the New York Giants. Washington Commanders Get Good Injury News in the Secondary - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Washington Commanders Get Good Injury News in the Secondary (Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images) Ahmed Ghafir Thu, October 15, 2026 at 6:51 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads With the page turned to week six, the Washington Commanders got good news in the secondary on the injury front ahead of Thursday's practice. Head coach Dan Quinn noted that both cornerback Trey Amos and safety Nick Cross will have full practices this week, marking a welcomed development for an inconsistent and, at times, thin secondary. Amos has yet to appear in a game since week ten of his rookie season after suffering a fractured fibula in the midst of a breakout season, though also the start of what has proven to be a long road to recovery. Amos was also placed on the PUP list prior to training camp, then placed him on injured reserve ahead of the regular season opener after appearing for all of 30 minutes during practice in August. Cross, meanwhile, suffered an internal injury in the week two loss where he was hospitalized following the game then discharged the following day. The Bowie, Md. native has been sidelined since then before proving himself as an impact piece under defensive coordinator Daronte Jones. Quinn also revealed that running back Jeremy McNichols is expected to join Amos and Cross with a full week of practice, giving a potential shakeup to the running back rotation in week six. McNichols joined Amos on the reserve/injured list to open the regular season after suffering a quad injury during preseason, paving the way for rookie Kaytron Allen to make the initial 53-man roster before being waived last week then claimed by the Miami Dolphins the following day. away.blurb: In fact, Big Blue might be the healthier team on Sunday. The Washington Commanders are dealing with a long list of injuries, even with Jayden Daniels likely set to return to the field. His teammates, on the other hand, have not had such an encouraging week. His top two receivers, Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, did not participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday. McLaurin participated in a limited capacity on Friday, but Diggs did not. Both wideouts are dealing with hamstring injuries. If McLaurin and Diggs are both out, Washington will be left with Dyami Brown, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, and Luke McCaffrey as its only healthy receivers. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a leg up in Week 5, even with Jayden Daniels Skip to main content News It may feel like the New York Giants are the most injured team in the NFL. They are not. Losing Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns, among others, for the season was a devastating blow, but the G-Men still have enough healthy talent on both sides of the ball to remain competitive, especially in a wide-open NFC East. With key commanders missing from the lineup, the Giants have an important advantage in what has become a crucial game in the NFC East title race. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs headline Commanders' injury report vs. Giants Daniels was a full participant in Commanders practice on both Wednesday and Thursday. Barring an unexpected change over the weekend, he should be able to play for the first time since injuring his elbow in Week 2. Of course, the Giants have some important injuries of their own. Braxton Berrios is now set to miss the season with a foot injury. Chauncey Golston's neck injury could leave New York thin on the edge, and safety Jason Pinnock is dealing with a concussion. But in terms of new names popping up on the injury report, the Giants certainly have the advantage in this game. Commanders' injury report gives Giants a clear advantage in Week 5 The Giants' secondary hasn't been stellar this season. The pass defense has been average in most categories and has been torn apart by the most efficient passing offenses it has faced. But if Washington is without its top two wide receivers, New York's secondary should be able to take control of the game. Deonte Banks, who has been a full participant in practice this week , and Greg Newsome II can lock Brown and Burks down on the outside while Dru Phillips handles Williams in the slot. If the Giants limit the Commanders' rushing attack, which hasn't been particularly efficient this year, they can put this game away early.

home.blurb: Mike Evans and Christian McCaffrey were among nine San Francisco 49ers who did not practice Thursday as the team prepares to host the Washington Commanders on Monday night, per the team's practice report. Seven others were limited: FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee), WR Christian Kirk (calf), T Colton McKivitz (illness), S Siran Neal (neck), CB Upton Stout (shoulder), DE Mykel Williams (knee) and G Carver Willis (toe). Kirk has been designated to return from injured reserve . Williams, like McCaffrey, is listed as a resting player. He was banged up with a neck injury earlier this season. Juszczyk, Sigle and Stout all left the 49ers’ Week 4 win over the Denver Broncos , but it's good to see them at least getting limited sessions in. Juszczyk, who missed Week 5, is expected to be out for a few weeks after his knee injury against the Broncos. Evans is listed with ribs and Achilles injuries. He has dealt with the rib issue since Week 3, but the Achilles designation is new . McCaffrey is listed as a rest day and not related to an injury. Here’s who did not participate Thursday: RB Christian McCaffrey (resting player) LT Trent Williams (resting player) Bosa and Samuel weren't surprises given Samuel injured his hamstring in Week 5 and was a possible injured reserve candidate and Bosa is still recovering from his calf injury. The Halton injury seems to be new, though. WR Jacob Cowing (ankle) and DE Romello Height (hand) were full participants. Dre Greenlaw is not on the report, but he is serving a one-game suspension Monday night after the NFL upheld his punishment for headbutting a Seahawks player. By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.
